"**Fortnight**" is a song by the American singer-songwriter [Taylor Swift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift "Taylor Swift") featuring the American musician [Post Malone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone "Post Malone"). It was written by the artists alongside [Jack Antonoff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Antonoff "Jack Antonoff"), who produced it with Swift. "Fortnight" is a 1980s-inspired [synth-pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synth-pop "Synth-pop"), [downtempo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Downtempo "Downtempo"), [electropop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electropop "Electropop"), [adult contemporary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adult_contemporary "Adult contemporary"), and [new wave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_wave_music "New wave music") [ballad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sentimental_ballad "Sentimental ballad") built around a steady, pulsing [synth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synth "Synth") [bassline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bassline "Bassline"), concluding with a [bridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bridge_\(music\) "Bridge (music)")\-like [outro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conclusion_\(music\) "Conclusion (music)") blending Swift and Malone's [vocal harmonies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vocal_harmonies "Vocal harmonies"). The lyrics describe an emotionally impactful romance that lasts for [two weeks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fortnight "Fortnight"): a woman in an unhappy marriage rekindles with a married ex-lover, and the two vow to escape to [Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida "Florida").

[Republic Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_Records "Republic Records") released "Fortnight" to mainstream radio as the [lead single](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lead_single "Lead single") from Swift's eleventh studio album, _[The Tortured Poets Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Tortured_Poets_Department "The Tortured Poets Department")_, on April 19, 2024. Reviews mostly praised the vocal chemistry between Swift and Malone but were mixed on the production; some reviews deemed it nuanced and catchy, but others described it as dull and derivative. The single peaked atop the [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") in the United States, the [_Billboard_ Global 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Global_200 "Billboard Global 200") chart, and the charts in Australia, Canada, Malaysia, New Zealand, the Philippines, Singapore, the United Arab Emirates, and the United Kingdom. At the [67th Annual Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "67th Annual Grammy Awards") in 2025, "Fortnight" was nominated for [Song of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Song_of_the_Year "Song of the Year") and [Record of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Record_of_the_Year "Record of the Year").

Swift directed the [music video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_video "Music video") for "Fortnight", collaborating with the Mexican cinematographer [Rodrigo Prieto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rodrigo_Prieto "Rodrigo Prieto"). Shot in black-and-white, the video portrays Swift as a mentally deranged patient in [Victorian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victorian_fashion "Victorian fashion")\-[gothic fashion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gothic_fashion "Gothic fashion") mourning a past relationship and reliving its memories. It stars Malone as her lover, and the _[Dead Poets Society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dead_Poets_Society "Dead Poets Society")_ co-stars [Ethan Hawke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethan_Hawke "Ethan Hawke") and [Josh Charles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josh_Charles "Josh Charles") as [mad scientists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mad_scientist "Mad scientist") experimenting on her. The video was met with critical praise and garnered a number of accolades, including Best Music Video at the [32nd Camerimage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/32nd_International_Film_Festival_of_the_Art_of_Cinematography_Camerimage "32nd International Film Festival of the Art of Cinematography Camerimage") festival, five wins including [Video of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Video_Music_Award_for_Video_of_the_Year "MTV Video Music Award for Video of the Year") at the [2024 MTV Video Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_MTV_Video_Music_Awards "2024 MTV Video Music Awards"), and [Best Video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Europe_Music_Award_for_Best_Song "MTV Europe Music Award for Best Song") at the [2024 MTV Europe Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_MTV_Europe_Music_Awards "2024 MTV Europe Music Awards").

## Background and release

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Fortnight_\(song\)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background and release")\]

The American singer-songwriter [Taylor Swift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift "Taylor Swift") developed her eleventh studio album, _[The Tortured Poets Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Tortured_Poets_Department "The Tortured Poets Department")_, as an introspective body of work that reflected "events, opinions and sentiments from a fleeting and fatalistic moment in time—one that was both sensational and sorrowful in equal measure".[\[1\]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEZaleski2024234-1) She wrote and recorded it throughout the 2023 run of [the Eras Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Eras_Tour "The Eras Tour"), amidst intense media reports on her personal life, including a breakup after a long-term relationship with [Joe Alwyn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Alwyn "Joe Alwyn") and a short-lived romantic relationship with [Matty Healy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matty_Healy "Matty Healy").[\[2\]](#cite_note-Sisario-2024-2)[\[3\]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTESomvilleBenoit2025437Zaleski2024234-3)

Swift announced _The Tortured Poets Department_ at the [66th Annual Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/66th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "66th Annual Grammy Awards") on February 4, 2024,[\[4\]](#cite_note-4) and unveiled the track listing via social media the following day. "Fortnight" is the opening track on the album, with [Post Malone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone "Post Malone") as the featured artist.[\[5\]](#cite_note-Tracklist-5) Swift brought the track to Malone's home studio in Los Angeles, and he recorded his background vocals and additional [hooks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hook_\(music\) "Hook (music)") for the [bridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bridge_\(music\) "Bridge (music)").[\[6\]](#cite_note-Coscarelli-2024-6) During an interview with [Zane Lowe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zane_Lowe "Zane Lowe") for [Apple Music 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_Music_1 "Apple Music 1") in February 2024, Malone said that he had not heard the full song.[\[7\]](#cite_note-7)

[![Swift standing on a bed onstage](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/01/Taylor_Swift_Eras_Tour_TTPD_Set_Fortnight.jpg/250px-Taylor_Swift_Eras_Tour_TTPD_Set_Fortnight.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Taylor_Swift_Eras_Tour_TTPD_Set_Fortnight.jpg)

Swift performing "Fortnight" for _[The Tortured Poets Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Tortured_Poets_Department "The Tortured Poets Department")_ act on [the Eras Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Eras_Tour "The Eras Tour"), on a bed emblazoned with the album's logo

"Fortnight" was released as the [lead single](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lead_single "Lead single") of _The Tortured Poets Department_ on April 19, 2024, concurrently with the album's release;[\[8\]](#cite_note-Denis-2024-8)[\[9\]](#cite_note-9) it was released to United States [contemporary hit radio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contemporary_hit_radio "Contemporary hit radio") and [hot adult contemporary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot_adult_contemporary "Hot adult contemporary") radio by [Republic Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_Records "Republic Records"),[\[10\]](#cite_note-Hits-2024-10) Italian [radio airplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radio_airplay "Radio airplay") by [Universal Music Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_Music_Group "Universal Music Group"),[\[11\]](#cite_note-Dragone-2024-11) and Canadian radio airplay by Republic/Universal.[\[12\]](#cite_note-:0-12) Swift unveiled the cover artwork via social media; it is a [grayscale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grayscale "Grayscale") photograph of Swift resting her cheek on a closed fist and Malone gazing into the camera with his hands clasped.[\[8\]](#cite_note-Denis-2024-8) The track was made available for purchase as a limited-time [CD single](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CD_single "CD single") through Swift's online store in the United States, Ireland, the United Kingdom, Germany, and Switzerland.[\[a\]](#cite_note-16) A remix by [Blond:ish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blond:ish "Blond:ish") was released on May 21,[\[16\]](#cite_note-Blond:ish_remix-17) and an acoustic version and a remix by [Cults](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cults_\(band\) "Cults (band)") followed on July 9, 2024.[\[17\]](#cite_note-acoustic_version-18) A special [7-inch vinyl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/7-inch_vinyl "7-inch vinyl") edition was released on April 12, 2025, to commemorate [Record Store Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Record_Store_Day "Record Store Day").[\[18\]](#cite_note-RecordStoreDay-19)

Starting from the Eras Tour shows in May 2024 in Paris, Swift revamped the set list to include songs from _The Tortured Poets Department_, including "Fortnight".[\[19\]](#cite_note-20)[\[20\]](#cite_note-21) For the performance of "Fortnight", the stage featured a "TTPD"-emblazoned bed and dancers dressed as nurses. Swift sang the song as she sat on a typewriter, across from a dancer, and the bed, which also resembled an office desk, moved across the stage.[\[21\]](#cite_note-22)[\[22\]](#cite_note-23)

## Production and music

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Fortnight_\(song\)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Production and music")\]

Swift and Malone wrote "Fortnight" with [Jack Antonoff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Antonoff "Jack Antonoff"), who [programmed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Programming_\(music\) "Programming (music)") the track and played acoustic guitar, electric guitar, the [Juno](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roland_Juno-60 "Roland Juno-60"), the [M1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korg_M1 "Korg M1"), drums, and percussion. [Sean Hutchinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Hutchinson "Sean Hutchinson") played additional drums, which were recorded by himself and [Michael Riddleberger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Riddleberger "Michael Riddleberger") at Hutchinson Sounds in Brooklyn. Malone's vocals were recorded and produced by [Louis Bell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_Bell "Louis Bell") at Electric Feel Studios in Los Angeles. "Fortnight" was produced by Swift and Antonoff; recorded by Laura Sisk and [Oli Jacobs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oli_Jacobs "Oli Jacobs") at [Conway Recording Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conway_Recording_Studios "Conway Recording Studios") in Los Angeles and [Electric Lady Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electric_Lady_Studios "Electric Lady Studios") in New York City; and [mixed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Audio_mixing_\(recorded_music\) "Audio mixing (recorded music)") by [Serban Ghenea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serban_Ghenea "Serban Ghenea") at Mixstar Studios in [Virginia Beach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia_Beach "Virginia Beach").[\[23\]](#cite_note-liner-24)

![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cb/Gnome-mime-audio-openclipart.svg/60px-Gnome-mime-audio-openclipart.svg.png)

A sample of "Fortnight", showing the pulsing [synth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synth "Synth") [bassline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bassline "Bassline"), Swift's monotonic vocals, and Malone's backing vocals in the lyric, "I love you, it's ruining my life."

"Fortnight" is 3 minutes and 48 seconds long.[\[23\]](#cite_note-liner-24) It is a 1980s-influenced [ballad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sentimental_ballad "Sentimental ballad") that incorporates [synth-pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synth-pop "Synth-pop"),[\[24\]](#cite_note-Clash-25)[\[25\]](#cite_note-Camp-2024-26)[\[26\]](#cite_note-Sheffield-2024-27) [downtempo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Downtempo "Downtempo"),[\[27\]](#cite_note-Hodgkinson-2024-28)[\[28\]](#cite_note-Richardson-2024-29) [electropop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electropop "Electropop"),[\[29\]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEZaleski2024-30)[\[30\]](#cite_note-31) [adult contemporary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adult_contemporary "Adult contemporary"),[\[31\]](#cite_note-Gaca-2025-32) and [new wave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_wave_music "New wave music").[\[32\]](#cite_note-33) Set over a [tempo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tempo "Tempo") of 96 beats per minute, the track begins with a [minimalist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minimal_music "Minimal music"), [electronic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_music "Electronic music") arrangement of M1 synthesizer backing, Juno synthesizer [sequence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sequence_\(music\) "Sequence (music)"), and Swift's vocals sung in a monotone.[\[33\]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTESomvilleBenoit2025440-34)[\[34\]](#cite_note-Lipshutz-2024-35) The rhythm is punctuated by [drum machine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drum_machine "Drum machine") beats and a pulsing [eighth-note](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eighth-note "Eighth-note") [synth bass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synth_bass "Synth bass") generated by [8-bit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/8-bit "8-bit") synth plucks[\[33\]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTESomvilleBenoit2025440-34)[\[35\]](#cite_note-Bannikov-2024-36)[\[36\]](#cite_note-Petridis-37) that repeat every eight [bars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bar_\(music\) "Bar (music)").[\[37\]](#cite_note-:1-38)

In the [refrain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Refrain "Refrain"), the lyric, "I love you, it's ruining my life", features Swift's lead vocals accompanied by Malone's echoing backing vocals.[\[38\]](#cite_note-Rosenbloom-2024-39)[\[39\]](#cite_note-Pareles-2024-40) After the first refrain, the arrangement becomes progressively dense, with thicker layers of synthesizer backing and louder drums.[\[33\]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTESomvilleBenoit2025440-34) The second refrain, starting at 1 minute and 43 seconds, features an additional layer of [snare drum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snare_drum "Snare drum") and [hi-hat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hi-hat "Hi-hat").[\[37\]](#cite_note-:1-38) Towards the concluding bridge, which also serves as the [outro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outro_\(music\) "Outro (music)"), Malone and Swift deliver [vocal harmonies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vocal_harmonies "Vocal harmonies"); the former sings lead vocals in the outro's first half, and the latter in the second half.[\[33\]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTESomvilleBenoit2025440-34)[\[34\]](#cite_note-Lipshutz-2024-35)[\[39\]](#cite_note-Pareles-2024-40) According to the music critic [Annie Zaleski](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annie_Zaleski "Annie Zaleski"), Swift sounds "seething and resigned", while Malone adds a sense of longing with his "earnest, buttery-smooth melodic counterpoints".[\[29\]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEZaleski2024-30)

Some critics opined that "Fortnight" was sonically similar to the muted pop sound of Swift's 2022 album _[Midnights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midnights "Midnights")_.[\[b\]](#cite_note-45) [_Clash_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clash_\(magazine\) "Clash (magazine)")'s Lauren Webb wrote that the track has a 1980s [power ballad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Power_ballad "Power ballad") sensibility reminiscent of such artists as [Roxette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roxette "Roxette"), [Cutting Crew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cutting_Crew "Cutting Crew"), and [Phil Collins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phil_Collins "Phil Collins"),[\[24\]](#cite_note-Clash-25) and _[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Guardian "The Guardian")_'s Laura Snapes thought that the "burbling synths, booming drums and glazed backing vocals" evoked the music of [the 1975](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_1975 "The 1975").[\[44\]](#cite_note-46) There were also multiple comparisons to the music of [Lana Del Rey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lana_Del_Rey "Lana Del Rey"),[\[27\]](#cite_note-Hodgkinson-2024-28)[\[45\]](#cite_note-47)[\[46\]](#cite_note-48) which _[American Songwriter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Songwriter "American Songwriter")_'s Thom Donovan described as "bleak [Americana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Americana_music "Americana music")".[\[43\]](#cite_note-Donovan-2024-44)

## Lyrics and interpretations

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Fortnight_\(song\)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Lyrics and interpretations")\]

The lyrics of "Fortnight" are about the strong impacts of a two-week romance that leaves behind fleeting emotions:[\[29\]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEZaleski2024-30) Swift's narrator is a woman in an unhappy marriage, and she becomes a neighbor of an ex-lover, who is now married to another woman.[\[27\]](#cite_note-Hodgkinson-2024-28)[\[47\]](#cite_note-Breihan-49) They encounter each other on a daily basis in a suburban American town, watering the flowers in their garden and chatting about the weather.[\[29\]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEZaleski2024-30) That she lives next door to her ex-lover makes her fantasize about killing the wife[\[43\]](#cite_note-Donovan-2024-44) and resort to alcoholism to cope with her misery.[\[29\]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEZaleski2024-30) In the double chorus that follows the second verse, Swift's character finds out about her husband's infidelity and desires to kill him also.[\[43\]](#cite_note-Donovan-2024-44) In the conclusion, Malone's character, representing the ex-lover of Swift's character, fantasizes about escaping to [Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida "Florida") with her to escape the torturous reality that they are in.[\[43\]](#cite_note-Donovan-2024-44)

Some publications highlighted that the title is a [British English](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_English "British English") noun meaning two weeks, possibly referencing Swift's previous romances with British men;[\[c\]](#cite_note-53) [Google searches](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_search "Google search") for the definition of "fortnight" in the United States increased by 868% on the song's release day.[\[51\]](#cite_note-54) Swift said that the track features many characteristics that define _The Tortured Poets Department_, including themes of "fatalism, longing, pining away, lost dreams"[\[52\]](#cite_note-55) and hyperbolic and dramatic lyrics ("I love you, it's ruining my life").[\[53\]](#cite_note-56) Explaining her songwriting perspective to [Amazon Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amazon_Music "Amazon Music"), she said that she imagined the setting of "Fortnight" as an American town where one's [American Dream](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Dream "American Dream") never materialized: "You ended up not with the person that you loved and now you just have to live with that every day, wondering what would've been maybe seeing them out."[\[54\]](#cite_note-57)

Several journalists suggested that "Fortnight" is autobiographical in nature, but it also blends confessional and fictional elements.[\[55\]](#cite_note-Brown-58)[\[56\]](#cite_note-D’Souza1-59)[\[57\]](#cite_note-60) The short-lived yet emotionally impactful romance in "Fortnight" becomes the subject of many other album tracks, and its imagery of violence and death (such as the narrator fantasizing about murdering the ex-lover's wife and her own cheating husband) also recurs in them.[\[58\]](#cite_note-61)[\[59\]](#cite_note-62)[\[60\]](#cite_note-63) [Rob Sheffield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rob_Sheffield "Rob Sheffield") of _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone "Rolling Stone")_ opined that the "1950s bad-marriage theme" of unhappy suburban marriages with cheating husbands and dutiful housewives "on the verge of nervous breakdowns" was reminiscent of Swift's songwriting for her past albums, [_Folklore_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Folklore_\(Taylor_Swift_album\) "Folklore (Taylor Swift album)"), _[Evermore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evermore "Evermore")_, and _Midnights_.[\[26\]](#cite_note-Sheffield-2024-27) Donovan described the scenario of "Fortnight" as a "suburban nightmare".[\[43\]](#cite_note-Donovan-2024-44) _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Times "The New York Times")_' Lindsay Zoladz thought that the track is "chilly and controlled" until it "\[thaws\] and \[glows\]" after the lyric, "I love you, it's ruining my life."[\[61\]](#cite_note-Zoladz-2024-64) _[USA Today](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USA_Today "USA Today")_'s Melissa Ruggeri dubbed the lyrics mentioning alcoholism as "darkly funny".[\[62\]](#cite_note-65)

[![Post Malone performing, singing onto a mic, dressed in checkered pants](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/99/Post_Malone_in_Chicago_2020.jpg/250px-Post_Malone_in_Chicago_2020.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Post_Malone_in_Chicago_2020.jpg)

Critics praised [Post Malone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone "Post Malone")'s guest vocals.

The track was picked as a highlight on _The Tortured Poets Department_ by Alli Rosenbloom of [CNN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CNN "CNN")[\[38\]](#cite_note-Rosenbloom-2024-39) and Mesfin Fekadu of _[The Hollywood Reporter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Hollywood_Reporter "The Hollywood Reporter")_.[\[42\]](#cite_note-Fekadu-2024-43) In _[PopMatters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PopMatters "PopMatters")_, Igor Bannikov lauded "Fortnight" as the best opening track of Swift's career for featuring a "delicate and cunning" songcraft with a "buoyant" synth-pop production, Swift's vocal harmonies, and self-referential lyricism.[\[35\]](#cite_note-Bannikov-2024-36) Webb and _[NME](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NME "NME")_'s Laura Molloy thought that the track displayed a new musical direction for Swift,[\[24\]](#cite_note-Clash-25)[\[63\]](#cite_note-NME-66) and _[The Irish Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Irish_Times "The Irish Times")_' Finn McRemmond praised the "impossible catchy hook" despite the dreary theme.[\[64\]](#cite_note-McRedmond1-67) Zoladz highlighted the lyrics for portraying "how viscerally Swift can summon the flushed delirium of a doomed romance".[\[61\]](#cite_note-Zoladz-2024-64)

Many critics praised the vocal chemistry between Swift and Malone. John Meagher of the _[Irish Independent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irish_Independent "Irish Independent")_ highlighted Malone's performance as more restrained compared to his usual "melodramatic" tendencies,[\[65\]](#cite_note-68) and Ed Power of _[The Daily Telegraph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Daily_Telegraph "The Daily Telegraph")_ wrote: "His breathy singing voice dovetails surprisingly with Swift's angsty coo."[\[66\]](#cite_note-Power-2024-69) [_Billboard_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard (magazine)")'s Jason Lipshutz ranked "Fortnight" fifth out of the 31 tracks on the [double album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Double_album "Double album") edition of _The Tortured Poets Department_, praising how Malone's appearance suits well with Swift's vocals and gives the bridge "subtle power and hangdog charm".[\[34\]](#cite_note-Lipshutz-2024-35) Bianca Gracie of [Grammy.com](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy.com "Grammy.com") also praised Malone's "melancholic harmonies" for giving "more emotional weight" to Swift's storytelling lyrics.[\[67\]](#cite_note-70)

Less enthusiastic reviews considered "Fortnight" a compositionally unmemorable song. Callie Ahlgrim of _[Business Insider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Business_Insider "Business Insider")_ deemed it uninventive and argued that it was too similar to Antonoff and Swift's previous collaborations, specifically calling it a derivative of _Midnights_.[\[41\]](#cite_note-Ahlgrim-20242-42) Mark Richardson of _[The Wall Street Journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Wall_Street_Journal "The Wall Street Journal")_ deemed it mediocre,[\[28\]](#cite_note-Richardson-2024-29) and [_Paste_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paste_\(magazine\) "Paste (magazine)") and Konstantinos Pappis from _[Our Culture Mag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Our_Culture_Mag "Our Culture Mag")_ criticized the sound as empty and bland.[\[68\]](#cite_note-Paste-71)[\[69\]](#cite_note-72) [_Variety_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variety_\(magazine\) "Variety (magazine)")'s Chris Willman regarded the single as a good choice for [pop radio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_radio "Pop radio"), but he contended that it was "not much of an indication of the more visceral, obsessive stuff" for the album's remainder.[\[40\]](#cite_note-Willman-2024-41) Alex Hudson of _[Exclaim!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exclaim! "Exclaim!")_ wrote that he was "genuinely shocked" that "such a dreary, unmemorable song" was released as a single.[\[70\]](#cite_note-Exclaim!-73)

_The Hollywood Reporter_ ranked "Fortnight" among their best songs of 2024.[\[71\]](#cite_note-74) _Billboard_ placed the song at number 10 on their list of the 100 best songs of the year.[\[72\]](#cite_note-75) At the [67th Annual Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "67th Annual Grammy Awards") in 2025, "Fortnight" was nominated for [Song of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Song_of_the_Year "Song of the Year") and [Record of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Record_of_the_Year "Record of the Year").[\[73\]](#cite_note-76)

## Commercial performance

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Fortnight_\(song\)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Commercial performance")\]

After one day of release, "Fortnight" set the [single-day streaming record for any song on Spotify](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Spotify_streaming_records#Most-streamed_songs_in_a_single_day "List of Spotify streaming records"), surpassing the all-time peak previously held by [Mariah Carey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mariah_Carey "Mariah Carey")'s song "[All I Want for Christmas Is You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_I_Want_for_Christmas_Is_You "All I Want for Christmas Is You")" (1994).[\[74\]](#cite_note-77) This achievement was registered in the _[Guinness World Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guinness_World_Records "Guinness World Records")_.[\[75\]](#cite_note-78)[\[76\]](#cite_note-79)[\[77\]](#cite_note-80) The single debuted atop the [_Billboard_ G

"**Fortnight**" is a song by the American singer-songwriter [Taylor Swift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift "Taylor Swift") featuring the American musician [Post Malone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone "Post Malone"). It was written by the artists alongside [Jack Antonoff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Antonoff "Jack Antonoff"), who produced it with Swift. "Fortnight" is a 1980s-inspired [synth-pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synth-pop "Synth-pop"), [downtempo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Downtempo "Downtempo"), [electropop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electropop "Electropop"), [adult contemporary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adult_contemporary "Adult contemporary"), and [new wave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_wave_music "New wave music") [ballad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sentimental_ballad "Sentimental ballad") built around a steady, pulsing [synth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synth "Synth") [bassline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bassline "Bassline"), concluding with a [bridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bridge_\(music\) "Bridge (music)")\-like [outro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conclusion_\(music\) "Conclusion (music)") blending Swift and Malone's [vocal harmonies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vocal_harmonies "Vocal harmonies"). The lyrics describe an emotionally impactful romance that lasts for [two weeks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fortnight "Fortnight"): a woman in an unhappy marriage rekindles with a married ex-lover, and the two vow to escape to [Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida "Florida").

[Republic Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_Records "Republic Records") released "Fortnight" to mainstream radio as the [lead single](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lead_single "Lead single") from Swift's eleventh studio album, _[The Tortured Poets Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Tortured_Poets_Department "The Tortured Poets Department")_, on April 19, 2024. Reviews mostly praised the vocal chemistry between Swift and Malone but were mixed on the production; some reviews deemed it nuanced and catchy, but others described it as dull and derivative. The single peaked atop the [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") in the United States, the [_Billboard_ Global 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Global_200 "Billboard Global 200") chart, and the charts in Australia, Canada, Malaysia, New Zealand, the Philippines, Singapore, the United Arab Emirates, and the United Kingdom. At the [67th Annual Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "67th Annual Grammy Awards") in 2025, "Fortnight" was nominated for [Song of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Song_of_the_Year "Song of the Year") and [Record of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Record_of_the_Year "Record of the Year").

Swift directed the [music video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_video "Music video") for "Fortnight", collaborating with the Mexican cinematographer [Rodrigo Prieto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rodrigo_Prieto "Rodrigo Prieto"). Shot in black-and-white, the video portrays Swift as a mentally deranged patient in [Victorian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victorian_fashion "Victorian fashion")\-[gothic fashion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gothic_fashion "Gothic fashion") mourning a past relationship and reliving its memories. It stars Malone as her lover, and the _[Dead Poets Society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dead_Poets_Society "Dead Poets Society")_ co-stars [Ethan Hawke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethan_Hawke "Ethan Hawke") and [Josh Charles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josh_Charles "Josh Charles") as [mad scientists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mad_scientist "Mad scientist") experimenting on her. The video was met with critical praise and garnered a number of accolades, including Best Music Video at the [32nd Camerimage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/32nd_International_Film_Festival_of_the_Art_of_Cinematography_Camerimage "32nd International Film Festival of the Art of Cinematography Camerimage") festival, five wins including [Video of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Video_Music_Award_for_Video_of_the_Year "MTV Video Music Award for Video of the Year") at the [2024 MTV Video Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_MTV_Video_Music_Awards "2024 MTV Video Music Awards"), and [Best Video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Europe_Music_Award_for_Best_Song "MTV Europe Music Award for Best Song") at the [2024 MTV Europe Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_MTV_Europe_Music_Awards "2024 MTV Europe Music Awards").

## Background and release

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Fortnight_\(song\)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background and release")\]

The American singer-songwriter [Taylor Swift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift "Taylor Swift") developed her eleventh studio album, _[The Tortured Poets Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Tortured_Poets_Department "The Tortured Poets Department")_, as an introspective body of work that reflected "events, opinions and sentiments from a fleeting and fatalistic moment in time—one that was both sensational and sorrowful in equal measure".[\[1\]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEZaleski2024234-1) She wrote and recorded it throughout the 2023 run of [the Eras Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Eras_Tour "The Eras Tour"), amidst intense media reports on her personal life, including a breakup after a long-term relationship with [Joe Alwyn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Alwyn "Joe Alwyn") and a short-lived romantic relationship with [Matty Healy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matty_Healy "Matty Healy").[\[2\]](#cite_note-Sisario-2024-2)[\[3\]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTESomvilleBenoit2025437Zaleski2024234-3)

Swift announced _The Tortured Poets Department_ at the [66th Annual Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/66th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "66th Annual Grammy Awards") on February 4, 2024,[\[4\]](#cite_note-4) and unveiled the track listing via social media the following day. "Fortnight" is the opening track on the album, with [Post Malone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone "Post Malone") as the featured artist.[\[5\]](#cite_note-Tracklist-5) Swift brought the track to Malone's home studio in Los Angeles, and he recorded his background vocals and additional [hooks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hook_\(music\) "Hook (music)") for the [bridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bridge_\(music\) "Bridge (music)").[\[6\]](#cite_note-Coscarelli-2024-6) During an interview with [Zane Lowe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zane_Lowe "Zane Lowe") for [Apple Music 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_Music_1 "Apple Music 1") in February 2024, Malone said that he had not heard the full song.[\[7\]](#cite_note-7)

[![Swift standing on a bed onstage](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/01/Taylor_Swift_Eras_Tour_TTPD_Set_Fortnight.jpg/250px-Taylor_Swift_Eras_Tour_TTPD_Set_Fortnight.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Taylor_Swift_Eras_Tour_TTPD_Set_Fortnight.jpg)

Swift performing "Fortnight" for _[The Tortured Poets Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Tortured_Poets_Department "The Tortured Poets Department")_ act on [the Eras Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Eras_Tour "The Eras Tour"), on a bed emblazoned with the album's logo

"Fortnight" was released as the [lead single](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lead_single "Lead single") of _The Tortured Poets Department_ on April 19, 2024, concurrently with the album's release;[\[8\]](#cite_note-Denis-2024-8)[\[9\]](#cite_note-9) it was released to United States [contemporary hit radio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contemporary_hit_radio "Contemporary hit radio") and [hot adult contemporary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot_adult_contemporary "Hot adult contemporary") radio by [Republic Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_Records "Republic Records"),[\[10\]](#cite_note-Hits-2024-10) Italian [radio airplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radio_airplay "Radio airplay") by [Universal Music Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_Music_Group "Universal Music Group"),[\[11\]](#cite_note-Dragone-2024-11) and Canadian radio airplay by Republic/Universal.[\[12\]](#cite_note-:0-12) Swift unveiled the cover artwork via social media; it is a [grayscale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grayscale "Grayscale") photograph of Swift resting her cheek on a closed fist and Malone gazing into the camera with his hands clasped.[\[8\]](#cite_note-Denis-2024-8) The track was made available for purchase as a limited-time [CD single](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CD_single "CD single") through Swift's online store in the United States, Ireland, the United Kingdom, Germany, and Switzerland.[\[a\]](#cite_note-16) A remix by [Blond:ish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blond:ish "Blond:ish") was released on May 21,[\[16\]](#cite_note-Blond:ish_remix-17) and an acoustic version and a remix by [Cults](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cults_\(band\) "Cults (band)") followed on July 9, 2024.[\[17\]](#cite_note-acoustic_version-18) A special [7-inch vinyl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/7-inch_vinyl "7-inch vinyl") edition was released on April 12, 2025, to commemorate [Record Store Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Record_Store_Day "Record Store Day").[\[18\]](#cite_note-RecordStoreDay-19)

Starting from the Eras Tour shows in May 2024 in Paris, Swift revamped the set list to include songs from _The Tortured Poets Department_, including "Fortnight".[\[19\]](#cite_note-20)[\[20\]](#cite_note-21) For the performance of "Fortnight", the stage featured a "TTPD"-emblazoned bed and dancers dressed as nurses. Swift sang the song as she sat on a typewriter, across from a dancer, and the bed, which also resembled an office desk, moved across the stage.[\[21\]](#cite_note-22)[\[22\]](#cite_note-23)

## Production and music

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Fortnight_\(song\)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Production and music")\]

Swift and Malone wrote "Fortnight" with [Jack Antonoff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Antonoff "Jack Antonoff"), who [programmed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Programming_\(music\) "Programming (music)") the track and played acoustic guitar, electric guitar, the [Juno](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roland_Juno-60 "Roland Juno-60"), the [M1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korg_M1 "Korg M1"), drums, and percussion. [Sean Hutchinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Hutchinson "Sean Hutchinson") played additional drums, which were recorded by himself and [Michael Riddleberger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Riddleberger "Michael Riddleberger") at Hutchinson Sounds in Brooklyn. Malone's vocals were recorded and produced by [Louis Bell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_Bell "Louis Bell") at Electric Feel Studios in Los Angeles. "Fortnight" was produced by Swift and Antonoff; recorded by Laura Sisk and [Oli Jacobs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oli_Jacobs "Oli Jacobs") at [Conway Recording Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conway_Recording_Studios "Conway Recording Studios") in Los Angeles and [Electric Lady Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electric_Lady_Studios "Electric Lady Studios") in New York City; and [mixed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Audio_mixing_\(recorded_music\) "Audio mixing (recorded music)") by [Serban Ghenea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serban_Ghenea "Serban Ghenea") at Mixstar Studios in [Virginia Beach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia_Beach "Virginia Beach").[\[23\]](#cite_note-liner-24)

![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cb/Gnome-mime-audio-openclipart.svg/60px-Gnome-mime-audio-openclipart.svg.png)

A sample of "Fortnight", showing the pulsing [synth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synth "Synth") [bassline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bassline "Bassline"), Swift's monotonic vocals, and Malone's backing vocals in the lyric, "I love you, it's ruining my life."

"Fortnight" is 3 minutes and 48 seconds long.[\[23\]](#cite_note-liner-24) It is a 1980s-influenced [ballad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sentimental_ballad "Sentimental ballad") that incorporates [synth-pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synth-pop "Synth-pop"),[\[24\]](#cite_note-Clash-25)[\[25\]](#cite_note-Camp-2024-26)[\[26\]](#cite_note-Sheffield-2024-27) [downtempo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Downtempo "Downtempo"),[\[27\]](#cite_note-Hodgkinson-2024-28)[\[28\]](#cite_note-Richardson-2024-29) [electropop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electropop "Electropop"),[\[29\]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEZaleski2024-30)[\[30\]](#cite_note-31) [adult contemporary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adult_contemporary "Adult contemporary"),[\[31\]](#cite_note-Gaca-2025-32) and [new wave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_wave_music "New wave music").[\[32\]](#cite_note-33) Set over a [tempo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tempo "Tempo") of 96 beats per minute, the track begins with a [minimalist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minimal_music "Minimal music"), [electronic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_music "Electronic music") arrangement of M1 synthesizer backing, Juno synthesizer [sequence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sequence_\(music\) "Sequence (music)"), and Swift's vocals sung in a monotone.[\[33\]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTESomvilleBenoit2025440-34)[\[34\]](#cite_note-Lipshutz-2024-35) The rhythm is punctuated by [drum machine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drum_machine "Drum machine") beats and a pulsing [eighth-note](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eighth-note "Eighth-note") [synth bass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synth_bass "Synth bass") generated by [8-bit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/8-bit "8-bit") synth plucks[\[33\]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTESomvilleBenoit2025440-34)[\[35\]](#cite_note-Bannikov-2024-36)[\[36\]](#cite_note-Petridis-37) that repeat every eight [bars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bar_\(music\) "Bar (music)").[\[37\]](#cite_note-:1-38)

In the [refrain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Refrain "Refrain"), the lyric, "I love you, it's ruining my life", features Swift's lead vocals accompanied by Malone's echoing backing vocals.[\[38\]](#cite_note-Rosenbloom-2024-39)[\[39\]](#cite_note-Pareles-2024-40) After the first refrain, the arrangement becomes progressively dense, with thicker layers of synthesizer backing and louder drums.[\[33\]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTESomvilleBenoit2025440-34) The second refrain, starting at 1 minute and 43 seconds, features an additional layer of [snare drum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snare_drum "Snare drum") and [hi-hat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hi-hat "Hi-hat").[\[37\]](#cite_note-:1-38) Towards the concluding bridge, which also serves as the [outro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outro_\(music\) "Outro (music)"), Malone and Swift deliver [vocal harmonies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vocal_harmonies "Vocal harmonies"); the former sings lead vocals in the outro's first half, and the latter in the second half.[\[33\]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTESomvilleBenoit2025440-34)[\[34\]](#cite_note-Lipshutz-2024-35)[\[39\]](#cite_note-Pareles-2024-40) According to the music critic [Annie Zaleski](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annie_Zaleski "Annie Zaleski"), Swift sounds "seething and resigned", while Malone adds a sense of longing with his "earnest, buttery-smooth melodic counterpoints".[\[29\]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEZaleski2024-30)

Some critics opined that "Fortnight" was sonically similar to the muted pop sound of Swift's 2022 album _[Midnights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midnights "Midnights")_.[\[b\]](#cite_note-45) [_Clash_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clash_\(magazine\) "Clash (magazine)")'s Lauren Webb wrote that the track has a 1980s [power ballad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Power_ballad "Power ballad") sensibility reminiscent of such artists as [Roxette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roxette "Roxette"), [Cutting Crew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cutting_Crew "Cutting Crew"), and [Phil Collins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phil_Collins "Phil Collins"),[\[24\]](#cite_note-Clash-25) and _[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Guardian "The Guardian")_'s Laura Snapes thought that the "burbling synths, booming drums and glazed backing vocals" evoked the music of [the 1975](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_1975 "The 1975").[\[44\]](#cite_note-46) There were also multiple comparisons to the music of [Lana Del Rey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lana_Del_Rey "Lana Del Rey"),[\[27\]](#cite_note-Hodgkinson-2024-28)[\[45\]](#cite_note-47)[\[46\]](#cite_note-48) which _[American Songwriter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Songwriter "American Songwriter")_'s Thom Donovan described as "bleak [Americana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Americana_music "Americana music")".[\[43\]](#cite_note-Donovan-2024-44)

## Lyrics and interpretations

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Fortnight_\(song\)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Lyrics and interpretations")\]

The lyrics of "Fortnight" are about the strong impacts of a two-week romance that leaves behind fleeting emotions:[\[29\]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEZaleski2024-30) Swift's narrator is a woman in an unhappy marriage, and she becomes a neighbor of an ex-lover, who is now married to another woman.[\[27\]](#cite_note-Hodgkinson-2024-28)[\[47\]](#cite_note-Breihan-49) They encounter each other on a daily basis in a suburban American town, watering the flowers in their garden and chatting about the weather.[\[29\]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEZaleski2024-30) That she lives next door to her ex-lover makes her fantasize about killing the wife[\[43\]](#cite_note-Donovan-2024-44) and resort to alcoholism to cope with her misery.[\[29\]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEZaleski2024-30) In the double chorus that follows the second verse, Swift's character finds out about her husband's infidelity and desires to kill him also.[\[43\]](#cite_note-Donovan-2024-44) In the conclusion, Malone's character, representing the ex-lover of Swift's character, fantasizes about escaping to [Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida "Florida") with her to escape the torturous reality that they are in.[\[43\]](#cite_note-Donovan-2024-44)

Some publications highlighted that the title is a [British English](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_English "British English") noun meaning two weeks, possibly referencing Swift's previous romances with British men;[\[c\]](#cite_note-53) [Google searches](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_search "Google search") for the definition of "fortnight" in the United States increased by 868% on the song's release day.[\[51\]](#cite_note-54) Swift said that the track features many characteristics that define _The Tortured Poets Department_, including themes of "fatalism, longing, pining away, lost dreams"[\[52\]](#cite_note-55) and hyperbolic and dramatic lyrics ("I love you, it's ruining my life").[\[53\]](#cite_note-56) Explaining her songwriting perspective to [Amazon Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amazon_Music "Amazon Music"), she said that she imagined the setting of "Fortnight" as an American town where one's [American Dream](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Dream "American Dream") never materialized: "You ended up not with the person that you loved and now you just have to live with that every day, wondering what would've been maybe seeing them out."[\[54\]](#cite_note-57)

Several journalists suggested that "Fortnight" is autobiographical in nature, but it also blends confessional and fictional elements.[\[55\]](#cite_note-Brown-58)[\[56\]](#cite_note-D’Souza1-59)[\[57\]](#cite_note-60) The short-lived yet emotionally impactful romance in "Fortnight" becomes the subject of many other album tracks, and its imagery of violence and death (such as the narrator fantasizing about murdering the ex-lover's wife and her own cheating husband) also recurs in them.[\[58\]](#cite_note-61)[\[59\]](#cite_note-62)[\[60\]](#cite_note-63) [Rob Sheffield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rob_Sheffield "Rob Sheffield") of _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone "Rolling Stone")_ opined that the "1950s bad-marriage theme" of unhappy suburban marriages with cheating husbands and dutiful housewives "on the verge of nervous breakdowns" was reminiscent of Swift's songwriting for her past albums, [_Folklore_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Folklore_\(Taylor_Swift_album\) "Folklore (Taylor Swift album)"), _[Evermore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evermore "Evermore")_, and _Midnights_.[\[26\]](#cite_note-Sheffield-2024-27) Donovan described the scenario of "Fortnight" as a "suburban nightmare".[\[43\]](#cite_note-Donovan-2024-44) _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Times "The New York Times")_' Lindsay Zoladz thought that the track is "chilly and controlled" until it "\[thaws\] and \[glows\]" after the lyric, "I love you, it's ruining my life."[\[61\]](#cite_note-Zoladz-2024-64) _[USA Today](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USA_Today "USA Today")_'s Melissa Ruggeri dubbed the lyrics mentioning alcoholism as "darkly funny".[\[62\]](#cite_note-65)

[![Post Malone performing, singing onto a mic, dressed in checkered pants](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/99/Post_Malone_in_Chicago_2020.jpg/250px-Post_Malone_in_Chicago_2020.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Post_Malone_in_Chicago_2020.jpg)

Critics praised [Post Malone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone "Post Malone")'s guest vocals.

The track was picked as a highlight on _The Tortured Poets Department_ by Alli Rosenbloom of [CNN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CNN "CNN")[\[38\]](#cite_note-Rosenbloom-2024-39) and Mesfin Fekadu of _[The Hollywood Reporter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Hollywood_Reporter "The Hollywood Reporter")_.[\[42\]](#cite_note-Fekadu-2024-43) In _[PopMatters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PopMatters "PopMatters")_, Igor Bannikov lauded "Fortnight" as the best opening track of Swift's career for featuring a "delicate and cunning" songcraft with a "buoyant" synth-pop production, Swift's vocal harmonies, and self-referential lyricism.[\[35\]](#cite_note-Bannikov-2024-36) Webb and _[NME](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NME "NME")_'s Laura Molloy thought that the track displayed a new musical direction for Swift,[\[24\]](#cite_note-Clash-25)[\[63\]](#cite_note-NME-66) and _[The Irish Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Irish_Times "The Irish Times")_' Finn McRemmond praised the "impossible catchy hook" despite the dreary theme.[\[64\]](#cite_note-McRedmond1-67) Zoladz highlighted the lyrics for portraying "how viscerally Swift can summon the flushed delirium of a doomed romance".[\[61\]](#cite_note-Zoladz-2024-64)

Many critics praised the vocal chemistry between Swift and Malone. John Meagher of the _[Irish Independent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irish_Independent "Irish Independent")_ highlighted Malone's performance as more restrained compared to his usual "melodramatic" tendencies,[\[65\]](#cite_note-68) and Ed Power of _[The Daily Telegraph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Daily_Telegraph "The Daily Telegraph")_ wrote: "His breathy singing voice dovetails surprisingly with Swift's angsty coo."[\[66\]](#cite_note-Power-2024-69) [_Billboard_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard (magazine)")'s Jason Lipshutz ranked "Fortnight" fifth out of the 31 tracks on the [double album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Double_album "Double album") edition of _The Tortured Poets Department_, praising how Malone's appearance suits well with Swift's vocals and gives the bridge "subtle power and hangdog charm".[\[34\]](#cite_note-Lipshutz-2024-35) Bianca Gracie of [Grammy.com](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy.com "Grammy.com") also praised Malone's "melancholic harmonies" for giving "more emotional weight" to Swift's storytelling lyrics.[\[67\]](#cite_note-70)

Less enthusiastic reviews considered "Fortnight" a compositionally unmemorable song. Callie Ahlgrim of _[Business Insider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Business_Insider "Business Insider")_ deemed it uninventive and argued that it was too similar to Antonoff and Swift's previous collaborations, specifically calling it a derivative of _Midnights_.[\[41\]](#cite_note-Ahlgrim-20242-42) Mark Richardson of _[The Wall Street Journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Wall_Street_Journal "The Wall Street Journal")_ deemed it mediocre,[\[28\]](#cite_note-Richardson-2024-29) and [_Paste_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paste_\(magazine\) "Paste (magazine)") and Konstantinos Pappis from _[Our Culture Mag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Our_Culture_Mag "Our Culture Mag")_ criticized the sound as empty and bland.[\[68\]](#cite_note-Paste-71)[\[69\]](#cite_note-72) [_Variety_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variety_\(magazine\) "Variety (magazine)")'s Chris Willman regarded the single as a good choice for [pop radio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_radio "Pop radio"), but he contended that it was "not much of an indication of the more visceral, obsessive stuff" for the album's remainder.[\[40\]](#cite_note-Willman-2024-41) Alex Hudson of _[Exclaim!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exclaim! "Exclaim!")_ wrote that he was "genuinely shocked" that "such a dreary, unmemorable song" was released as a single.[\[70\]](#cite_note-Exclaim!-73)

_The Hollywood Reporter_ ranked "Fortnight" among their best songs of 2024.[\[71\]](#cite_note-74) _Billboard_ placed the song at number 10 on their list of the 100 best songs of the year.[\[72\]](#cite_note-75) At the [67th Annual Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "67th Annual Grammy Awards") in 2025, "Fortnight" was nominated for [Song of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Song_of_the_Year "Song of the Year") and [Record of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Record_of_the_Year "Record of the Year").[\[73\]](#cite_note-76)

## Commercial performance

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Fortnight_\(song\)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Commercial performance")\]

After one day of release, "Fortnight" set the [single-day streaming record for any song on Spotify](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Spotify_streaming_records#Most-streamed_songs_in_a_single_day "List of Spotify streaming records"), surpassing the all-time peak previously held by [Mariah Carey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mariah_Carey "Mariah Carey")'s song "[All I Want for Christmas Is You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_I_Want_for_Christmas_Is_You "All I Want for Christmas Is You")" (1994).[\[74\]](#cite_note-77) This achievement was registered in the _[Guinness World Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guinness_World_Records "Guinness World Records")_.[\[75\]](#cite_note-78)[\[76\]](#cite_note-79)[\[77\]](#cite_note-80) The single debuted atop the [_Billboard_ G
