Other promotional visuals for _Midnights_ also feature 1970s aesthetics.[\[86\]](#cite_note-91)[\[87\]](#cite_note-92) The photographs and videos that Swift posted onto social media featured a clock face, family-room furniture with retro [upholstery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upholstery "Upholstery"), and a [rust](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rust_\(color\) "Rust (color)") velvet curtain in the background.[\[42\]](#cite_note-Willman-2022c-43)[\[88\]](#cite_note-93)[\[89\]](#cite_note-94) Her wardrobe incorporated embellishments that [_Vogue_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vogue_\(magazine\) "Vogue (magazine)") identified as "disco [sequins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sequin "Sequin")" and "[corduroy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corduroy "Corduroy") flare".[\[90\]](#cite_note-95) The covers for three other physical editions all feature 1970s memorabilia: a retro piano, a [push-button telephone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Push-button_telephone "Push-button telephone"), and a [wood-paneled](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panelling "Panelling") wall.[\[76\]](#cite_note-Sanchez-2022-80)[\[80\]](#cite_note-Willman-2022a-84) Their reverse sides each portray a quarter sector of a dial and, when assembled together and combined with a [clock mechanism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clockwork "Clockwork") sold separately, form a functioning clock.[\[91\]](#cite_note-96) The [music videos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_video "Music video") for "Anti-Hero", "Bejeweled", and "Lavender Haze" feature Swift in [1970s fashion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1970s_fashion "1970s fashion"): [houndstooth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houndstooth "Houndstooth") polo sweaters, ribbed knit trousers, and sequined bodysuits.[\[f\]](#cite_note-100)

Swift extensively used social media to promote _Midnights_.[\[1\]](#cite_note-Lutz-2022-1)[\[8\]](#cite_note-Martoccio-2022-8) After the announcement at the MTV Video Music Awards, Swift's website and the canvases of her songs on [Spotify](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spotify "Spotify") were updated with images of a clock.[\[95\]](#cite_note-101) Using the video-sharing platform [TikTok](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TikTok "TikTok"), from September 21 to October 7, 2022, she released a 13-episode video series called _Midnights Mayhem with Me_, where she announced the title of each track in a randomized order per episode.[\[96\]](#cite_note-Jones-2022-102) In each episode, Swift rolled a [lottery cage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lottery_machine#Gravity_Pick "Lottery machine") containing 13 ping pong balls numbered from 1 to 13, each representing a track of the album; when a ball dropped out, she disclosed the title of the corresponding track through a telephone.[\[97\]](#cite_note-103)[\[96\]](#cite_note-Jones-2022-102) On October 17, Swift posted on her social media an itinerary titled _Midnights Manifest_, which included promotional events she had planned.[\[98\]](#cite_note-104) Swift partnered with Spotify to display some lyrics from _Midnights_ on billboards in five cities: New York, London, [São Paulo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/São_Paulo "São Paulo"), Nashville, and Mexico City.[\[99\]](#cite_note-105) Another partnership with [Apple Fitness+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fitness_\(Apple\) "Fitness (Apple)") included three exercise programs designed around Swift's music, featuring tracks from _Midnights_.[\[100\]](#cite_note-106)

Although Swift extensively promoted _Midnights_ and announced multiple release pre-orders, she did not conduct press interviews or preview music prior to the album's release.[\[2\]](#cite_note-Snapes-2022-2) [Republic Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_Records "Republic Records") released _Midnights_ on October 21, 2022.[\[48\]](#cite_note-Sisario-2022-49) The standard edition was made available for streaming, download, cassette, four CD variants, and four [vinyl LP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vinyl_LP "Vinyl LP") variants.[\[101\]](#cite_note-107) [Target](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Target_Corporation "Target Corporation") stores exclusively sold a _Lavender Edition_ on CD and vinyl LP, and [Capital One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capital_One "Capital One") distributed a [box set](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Box_set "Box set") that contained the CD and a Swift-branded T-shirt.[\[102\]](#cite_note-Caulfield-2022b-108) The _3am Edition_ was surprise-released onto streaming and digital services three hours after the standard edition.[\[102\]](#cite_note-Caulfield-2022b-108) From October 21 to 26, [iHeartRadio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IHeartRadio "IHeartRadio") aired a program called _iHeartRadio Brings You Midnights with Taylor_, which featured tracks from the album and stories behind the songs told by Swift herself.[\[103\]](#cite_note-109) She appeared, but did not perform, on the talk shows _[The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Tonight_Show_Starring_Jimmy_Fallon "The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon")_ on October 24[\[104\]](#cite_note-110) and _[The Graham Norton Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Graham_Norton_Show "The Graham Norton Show")_ on October 28.[\[105\]](#cite_note-111)

[![Swift, dressed in a rhinestoned bodysuite, singing into a mic](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5d/Taylor_Swift_The_Eras_Tour_Midnights_Era_Set_%2853109799784%29_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Taylor_Swift_The_Eras_Tour_Midnights_Era_Set_%2853109799784%29_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Taylor_Swift_The_Eras_Tour_Midnights_Era_Set_\(53109799784\)_\(cropped\).jpg)

Swift performing on [the Eras Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Eras_Tour "The Eras Tour") at [SoFi Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SoFi_Stadium "SoFi Stadium") in August 2023

"Anti-Hero" was released as the album's lead single on October 21, 2022.[\[106\]](#cite_note-112) In the United States, it became the best-selling song of 2022[\[107\]](#cite_note-Caulfield-2023a-113) and made Swift the first artist to have a number-one song on the [Radio Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radio_Songs_\(chart\) "Radio Songs (chart)") chart in the 2000s, 2010s, and 2020s decades.[\[108\]](#cite_note-114) "Bejeweled" and "Question...?" were released for limited-time digital download exclusively through Swift's website on October 25.[\[109\]](#cite_note-115) "Snow on the Beach" was issued to US [triple-A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adult_album_alternative "Adult album alternative") radio as a single on November 7, 2022,[\[110\]](#cite_note-116) followed by the US [pop radio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_radio "Pop radio") releases of "Lavender Haze" on November 29, 2022,[\[111\]](#cite_note-117)[\[112\]](#cite_note-118) and "Karma" on May 1, 2023.[\[113\]](#cite_note-119)[\[114\]](#cite_note-120) A remix of "Karma" featuring the rapper [Ice Spice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ice_Spice "Ice Spice") was released on May 26, 2023.[\[115\]](#cite_note-121) On the US [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100"), "Anti-Hero" reached number one, "Lavender Haze" and "Karma" both peaked at number two, and "Snow on the Beach" charted at number four.[\[116\]](#cite_note-122)[\[117\]](#cite_note-Trust-2022-123)

The promotional rollout of _Midnights_ received media commentary. Unterberger and [_Slate_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slate_\(magazine\) "Slate (magazine)")'s Chris Molanphy described it as a middle ground between a traditional album rollout and the surprise-release strategy of _Folklore_ and _Evermore_.[\[118\]](#cite_note-Unterberger-2022b-124)[\[119\]](#cite_note-Molanphy-2022-125) Molanphy argued that _Midnights_ employed an optimal promotion for every consumption metric: the multiple CD and LP offers would boost physical sales, the limited-time download tracks would increase digital sales, and the surprise _3am Edition_ release would prompt higher streams.[\[119\]](#cite_note-Molanphy-2022-125) The fact that there were no pre-release singles prompted speculation on the album's sound and content,[\[2\]](#cite_note-Snapes-2022-2)[\[118\]](#cite_note-Unterberger-2022b-124)[\[120\]](#cite_note-126) and the TikTok video series prompted Swift's fans to interpret possible [Easter eggs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_egg_\(media\) "Easter egg (media)"), heightening the anticipation for the album.[\[121\]](#cite_note-127)

To support _Midnights_ and her other albums, Swift embarked on [the Eras Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Eras_Tour "The Eras Tour"), which she described as a retrospective journey through her "musical eras".[\[122\]](#cite_note-128) Running from March 2023 to December 2024, the tour spanned 149 dates and visited five continents.[\[123\]](#cite_note-129) It became the first concert tour to gross over $1 billion, totaling $2 billion, the [highest-grossing in history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_highest-grossing_concert_tours "List of highest-grossing concert tours").[\[124\]](#cite_note-130) During the run of the tour, a _Til Dawn Edition_ of _Midnights_ containing the bonus track "[Hits Different](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hits_Different "Hits Different")" was released to digital platforms, and a _Late Night Edition_ containing the bonus track "[You're Losing Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/You're_Losing_Me "You're Losing Me")" was sold as concert–exclusive merchandise starting from the [East Rutherford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Rutherford "East Rutherford") show on May 26, 2023.[\[125\]](#cite_note-Caulfield-2023b-131)

## Commercial performance

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Midnights&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Commercial performance")\]

_Midnights_ was a commercial success across all consumption metrics: streaming, digital sales, and physical sales.[\[75\]](#cite_note-Unterberger-2022a-79)[\[126\]](#cite_note-132) It broke various records on music streaming platforms.[\[127\]](#cite_note-133) On Spotify, _Midnights_ broke records for the [highest single-day streams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_most-streamed_songs_on_Spotify#Most_streamed_albums_in_a_single_day "List of most-streamed songs on Spotify") and the highest single-week streams.[\[128\]](#cite_note-134)[\[129\]](#cite_note-Jericho-2022-135) It also claimed the highest single-day streams for a pop album and an album released in [Dolby Atmos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dolby_Atmos "Dolby Atmos") on [Apple Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_Music "Apple Music"), the highest single-week streams for an album on [Amazon Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amazon_Music "Amazon Music"), and the highest single-day requests on [Amazon Alexa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amazon_Alexa "Amazon Alexa").[\[130\]](#cite_note-Young-2022-136) All of its tracks entered the [_Billboard_ Global 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Global_200 "Billboard Global 200") simultaneously; it set the record for the most simultaneous top-10 entries (nine) and made Swift the first artist to occupy the entire top five.[\[131\]](#cite_note-137)

In the United States, _Midnights_ became Swift's record-extending fifth album to sell one million first-week copies after five days of availability.[\[132\]](#cite_note-138) It debuted atop the [_Billboard_ 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_200 "Billboard 200") with first-week units of 1.578 million, consisting of 1.14 million sales and 549.26 million streams,[\[133\]](#cite_note-Caulfield-2022a-139) tying her with [Barbra Streisand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbra_Streisand "Barbra Streisand") for the most number-one albums for a female artist (11).[\[133\]](#cite_note-Caulfield-2022a-139) _Midnights_ was the best-selling album of 2022, the second-best-selling album of 2023, and the second-most-consumed album of both years.[\[134\]](#cite_note-140) Swift became the first artist to have a [yearly best-seller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_best-selling_albums_by_year_in_the_United_States "List of best-selling albums by year in the United States") six times since [Luminate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luminate_\(company\) "Luminate (company)") tracked US music sales in 1991.[\[107\]](#cite_note-Caulfield-2023a-113) _Midnights_ spent six weeks atop the _Billboard_ 200,[\[125\]](#cite_note-Caulfield-2023b-131) and 68 weeks in the top 10, the longest run in the top 10 for Swift.[\[135\]](#cite_note-141) Its songs, led by "Anti-Hero", made Swift the first artist to occupy the entire top 10 of the _Billboard_ Hot 100 the same week;[\[117\]](#cite_note-Trust-2022-123) all 20 tracks from the _3am Edition_ charted in the top 45.[\[136\]](#cite_note-142) "Anti-Hero" and _Midnights_ marked the fourth time Swift had a number-one album and song simultaneously.[\[117\]](#cite_note-Trust-2022-123) It had sold 2.814 million US copies by January 2024.[\[137\]](#cite_note-143) In September 2025, the [Recording Industry Association of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recording_Industry_Association_of_America "Recording Industry Association of America") (RIAA) [certified](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RIAA_certification "RIAA certification") the album seven-times platinum, denoting seven million [album-equivalent units](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Album-equivalent_units "Album-equivalent units").[\[138\]](#cite_note-RIAA-144)

_Midnights_ debuted at number one on the album charts in at least 14 countries, including Belgium, Canada, Finland, France, Germany, Italy, Ireland, the Netherlands, New Zealand, Norway, and Sweden.[\[130\]](#cite_note-Young-2022-136) It was Swift's first number-one album in France and Germany[\[139\]](#cite_note-145)[\[140\]](#cite_note-146) and made her the best-selling foreign artist in China of 2022 after selling nearly 250,000 copies within one day.[\[141\]](#cite_note-147) On the [Australian charts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_charts "Australian charts"), _Midnights_ was Swift's 10th consecutive number-one album,[\[142\]](#cite_note-148) and its tracks made her the first artist to have nine songs on the top 10 of the singles chart the same week.[\[143\]](#cite_note-149) In the United Kingdom, _Midnights_ sold over 140,000 units in its first three days to become the fastest-selling album of 2022.[\[144\]](#cite_note-150) It debuted atop the [UK Albums Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Albums_Chart "UK Albums Chart") with 204,000 units, helping Swift achieve the shortest duration (10 years) for a female act to accumulate nine UK number-one albums.[\[145\]](#cite_note-151) _Midnights_ spent five weeks atop the UK Albums Chart.[\[146\]](#cite_note-152) It sold 80,000 vinyl copies in 2022, the highest annual figure for an album in the 21st century, propelling total UK vinyl sales past CD sales for the first time since 1987.[\[147\]](#cite_note-153)

According to [Universal Music Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_Music_Group "Universal Music Group"), the album crossed three million album-equivalent units in its first week and six million in two months.[\[148\]](#cite_note-154) [Bloomberg News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bloomberg_News "Bloomberg News") reported that the album generated $230 million in sales for Universal in 2022, accounting for 3% of their annual revenue—the highest from any artist.[\[149\]](#cite_note-155) The [International Federation of the Phonographic Industry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Federation_of_the_Phonographic_Industry "International Federation of the Phonographic Industry") (IFPI) recognized _Midnights_ as the second-most-consumed album of 2022; it ranked third in pure sales (first in vinyl sales) and fifth in streams; they named Swift the [Global Recording Artist of 2022](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_Recording_Artist_of_the_Year "Global Recording Artist of the Year"), which made her the first act to win the accolade three times (after 2014 and 2019).[\[150\]](#cite_note-156)[\[151\]](#cite_note-157) In the IFPI's 2023 report, _Midnights_ was the year's fourth-most-consumed album (third in bot

# The Tortured Poets Department

/en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J._M._Barrie "J. M. Barrie")'s 20th-century play and novel _[Peter Pan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Pan_\(play_and_novel\) "Peter Pan (play and novel)")_. Told from the perspective of [Wendy Darling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wendy_Darling "Wendy Darling"), the song depicts her waiting by the window for the day [Peter Pan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Pan_\(character\) "Peter Pan (character)") grows up and comes back to her. By the end of the song, in the [bridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bridge_\(music\) "Bridge (music)"), she concedes that she has tried in vain and, pleading with Peter Pan to forgive her, extinguishes the candlelight.[\[45\]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBurt2025-45)[\[55\]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMills2024237-55) "The Bolter" was influenced by [Nancy Mitford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Mitford "Nancy Mitford")'s 1945 novel _[The Pursuit of Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Pursuit_of_Love "The Pursuit of Love")_, about a female character nicknamed "The Bolter", who stays in society's margin and looks for love anywhere and in anyone. In her song, Swift's narrator is an endearing and mischievous woman who finds pleasure in seducing bad men, whom she describes as "trophy hunters", and escaping them at every turn.[\[48\]](#cite_note-Telegraph-48)[\[56\]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTESomvilleBenoit2025468-56)

Other tracks draw from Swift's self-awareness and fame. In "[How Did It End?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/How_Did_It_End%3F "How Did It End?")", her narrator explores anguish over a failed relationship and contemplates how the public's interest in her private life contributes to the distorted reality and gossip that ensue.[\[57\]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTESomvilleBenoit2025460-57) In "I Hate It Here", her narrator daydreams about escaping to an idealized past, imagining a beautiful landscape of secret gardens, lunar valleys, and gentle people, but she later acknowledges that nostalgia is a trap.[\[58\]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTESomvilleBenoit2025462-58) "[Thank You Aimee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thank_You_Aimee "Thank You Aimee")" is a sarcastic attack on a high-school bully; Swift's narrator appreciates the bully for making her stronger and tells them that she has changed their name so that they cannot enjoy the attention.[\[48\]](#cite_note-Telegraph-48) The closing track, "The Manuscript", is a re-examination of a long-gone romantic relationship with an older man; while it was once painful, Swift's narrator reflects on it with maturity and acceptance.[\[19\]](#cite_note-Wilson-2024-19)[\[48\]](#cite_note-Telegraph-48) She ends the song with the line, "The story isn't mine anymore." According to Mills, this lyric refers to the "[death of the author](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Death_of_the_author "Death of the author")"—by relinquishing authorship on her stories, Swift gives way for her audience to collectively construct and own theirs, thus positioning herself as a "modern-day Homer" and turning her songs into folktales.[\[55\]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMills2024237-55)

## Production and music

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=The_Tortured_Poets_Department&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Production and music")\]

_The Tortured Poets Department_ took two years to complete.[\[7\]](#cite_note-Martoccio-2024-7) Swift recorded and produced with Antonoff at [Electric Lady Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electric_Lady_Studios "Electric Lady Studios") in New York City and [Conway Recording Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conway_Recording_Studios "Conway Recording Studios") in Los Angeles, and with Dessner at Long Pond Studios in the [Hudson Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hudson_Valley "Hudson Valley"). "Fresh Out the Slammer", "Florida!!!", and "Who's Afraid of Little Old Me" were additionally recorded at Esplanade Studios in [New Orleans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Orleans "New Orleans"); "Florida!!!" also at [Miloco Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miloco_Studios "Miloco Studios") in London; and "I Can Fix Him (No Really I Can)" at Rue Boyer Studio A in [Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris "Paris").[\[9\]](#cite_note-Liner-9) On tracks co-produced with Antonoff, his bandmates from [Bleachers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bleachers_\(band\) "Bleachers (band)") played and recorded instruments at their respective studios: [Zem Audu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zem_Audu "Zem Audu") and [Evan Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evan_Smith_\(musician\) "Evan Smith (musician)") on [synthesizers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synthesizers "Synthesizers"), [Michael Riddleberger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Riddleberger "Michael Riddleberger") and [Sean Hutchinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Hutchinson "Sean Hutchinson") on drums and percussion, and [Mikey Freedom Hart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mikey_Freedom_Hart "Mikey Freedom Hart") on guitars and keyboards.[\[9\]](#cite_note-Liner-9)[\[59\]](#cite_note-59) Swift's vocals were recorded by Laura Sisk at Electric Lady, and by [Christopher Rowe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Rowe_\(music_producer\) "Christopher Rowe (music producer)") at Prime Recording Studio in [Nashville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nashville "Nashville").[\[9\]](#cite_note-Liner-9) Conducted by [Robert Ames](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Ames_\(conductor\) "Robert Ames (conductor)"), the [London Contemporary Orchestra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_Contemporary_Orchestra "London Contemporary Orchestra") provided [string sections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/String_section "String section") consisting of violins, violas, cellos, and [double basses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Double_bass "Double bass"), to "Clara Bow" on the standard edition,[\[60\]](#cite_note-60) and nine tracks on _The Anthology_.[\[61\]](#cite_note-61)

The music of _The Tortured Poets Department_ is [minimalist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minimalist_music "Minimalist music").[\[62\]](#cite_note-Keefe-2024-62)[\[63\]](#cite_note-Bannikov-63) Compositionally, the songs reprise many elements that had been characteristic of Swift's music: they employ the [verse-chorus form](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Verse-chorus_form "Verse-chorus form") largely composed in [major scale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_scale "Major scale") and set in [common time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Common_time "Common time"), one-note melodies in the verses that create tensions for more tuneful choruses, and [syncopated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syncopated "Syncopated") rhythms and phrasings.[\[64\]](#cite_note-Pareles-2024-64)[\[65\]](#cite_note-65) Many critics commented that the song structures and instrumental timbres feature influences of country music, a genre that defined her early career;[\[15\]](#cite_note-Brown-2024-15)[\[66\]](#cite_note-Petridis-66)[\[67\]](#cite_note-Foggart-67)[\[68\]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHughes2025132-68) according to [Jon Pareles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Pareles "Jon Pareles") of _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Times "The New York Times")_, Swift plays on traditional country songwriting by employing a "choppy pre-chorus, or chorus, that arrives in two-syllable bursts", which accentuates a steady verse structure and brings a "[hip-hop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hip-hop "Hip-hop") percussiveness".[\[64\]](#cite_note-Pareles-2024-64) Swift sings mostly in the lower ranges of her [vocal register](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vocal_register "Vocal register"), resulting in a [rap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rap "Rap")\-like, conversational delivery;[\[14\]](#cite_note-Powers-2024-14)[\[21\]](#cite_note-Leszkiewicz-21)[\[69\]](#cite_note-Breihan-2024-69) the music professor Samuel Murray commented that she reprised many of her common vocal devices, such as one-note melodies and a [recitative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recitative "Recitative") singing style.[\[36\]](#cite_note-Murray-36)

![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cb/Gnome-mime-audio-openclipart.svg/60px-Gnome-mime-audio-openclipart.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)

The production styles of Antonoff and Dessner result in two distinct soundscapes_.[\[23\]](#cite_note-Light-2024-23)_ Antonoff's synth-based approach results in [mid-tempo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mid-tempo "Mid-tempo") [synth-pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synth-pop "Synth-pop") songs that characterize the standard edition,[\[a\]](#cite_note-Synth-73)[\[73\]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTESomvilleBenoit2025439-74) with an [ambient](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ambient_music "Ambient music"), [electronica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronica "Electronica") soundscape composed of sustained [pads](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synth_pad "Synth pad") and [bass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synth_bass "Synth bass"),[\[15\]](#cite_note-Brown-2024-15)[\[21\]](#cite_note-Leszkiewicz-21)[\[74\]](#cite_note-Rogerson-2024-75) electronic [pulses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulse_\(music\) "Pulse (music)"),[\[23\]](#cite_note-Light-2024-23) and sparse, [programmed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Programming_\(music\) "Programming (music)") [drum machine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drum_machine "Drum machine") beats.[\[75\]](#cite_note-Horn-2024-76)[\[76\]](#cite_note-77) The compositions incorporate elements of country, [rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_music "Rock music"),[\[77\]](#cite_note-Kornhaber-78) [pop rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_rock "Pop rock"),[\[66\]](#cite_note-Petridis-66) [dream pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dream_pop "Dream pop"),[\[67\]](#cite_note-Foggart-67) and [sophisti-pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophisti-pop "Sophisti-pop").[\[78\]](#cite_note-Bridgewater-2024-79) According to music critics, _The Tortured Poets Department_ evokes the pop sounds of Swift's albums _Midnights_[\[b\]](#cite_note-80) and _[1989](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1989_\(album\) "1989 (album)")_ (2014),[\[c\]](#cite_note-81) but it is more muted and less danceable.[\[63\]](#cite_note-Bannikov-63)[\[79\]](#cite_note-82) Dessner's acoustic arrangements are driven by piano and guitar,[\[23\]](#cite_note-Light-2024-23)[\[32\]](#cite_note-BurtNation-32) resulting in mellow [folk-pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Folk-pop "Folk-pop") and [chamber pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chamber_pop "Chamber pop") [ballads](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sentimental_ballad "Sentimental ballad")[\[63\]](#cite_note-Bannikov-63)[\[73\]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTESomvilleBenoit2025439-74)[\[80\]](#cite_note-83) that characterize _The Anthology_,[\[49\]](#cite_note-Sheffield-Anthology-49)[\[81\]](#cite_note-Exclaim!-84) which also infuses elements of [soft rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soft_rock "Soft rock").[\[82\]](#cite_note-85) Critics compared this production style to his collaborations with Swift on her 2020 albums _[Folklore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Folklore_\(Taylor_Swift_album\) "Folklore (Taylor Swift album)")_ and _[Evermore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evermore "Evermore")_.[\[d\]](#cite_note-86)

The first five tracks of _The Tortured Poets Department_ exemplify the muted synth-pop sound: "Fortnight", "The Tortured Poets Department", "My Boy Only Breaks His Favorite Toys", "Down Bad" and "So Long, London".[\[83\]](#cite_note-Jenkins-87)[\[84\]](#cite_note-88) The first three incorporate influences of 1980s pop on their synth textures; "Fortnight" and "My Boy Only Breaks His Favorite Toys" incorporate an ambient, [new wave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_wave_music "New wave music") atmosphere.[\[85\]](#cite_note-89)[\[86\]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTESomvilleBenoit2025440,_442-90) "Down Bad" features [R&B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contemporary_R&B "Contemporary R&B") inflections in its dynamic shifts and vocal [cadences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cadence "Cadence").[\[77\]](#cite_note-Kornhaber-78) "So Long, London" begins with vocal harmonies that resemble a [cathedral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cathedral "Cathedral") choir and progresses into an electronic arrangement of trembling, fast-paced synths.[\[41\]](#cite_note-Snapes-41)[\[87\]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBurt2025Hughes2025132-91)

![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cb/Gnome-mime-audio-openclipart.svg/60px-Gnome-mime-audio-openclipart.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)

The next six tracks feature strong country influences, brought by a [twang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twang "Twang") in their instrumental timbres.[\[68\]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHughes2025132-68) "But Daddy I Love Him" combines country, [folk rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Folk_rock "Folk rock"), and [electropop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electropop "Electropop"), over amplified [snare drums](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snare_drum "Snare drum"), dynamic strings, and Swift's full voice in her upper register.[\[88\]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHughes2025133SomvilleBenoit2025445-92) The [reverbed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reverb_effect "Reverb effect") [electric guitar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electric_guitar "Electric guitar") in "Fresh Out the Slammer" evokes [Americana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Americana_music "Americana music"), while the composition of "Florida!!!"—gentle synths and rhythmic programming in the verses, and loud synths in the choruses, which end with a deep, [tremolo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tremolo "Tremolo") electric guitar—situates it within [indie rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indie_rock "Indie rock") and [arena rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arena_rock "Arena rock").[\[89\]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHughes2025133–134SomvilleBenoit2025447-93) "Guilty as Sin?" infuses elements of pop rock and 1990s soft rock,[\[37\]](#cite_note-Hodgkinson-37)[\[90\]](#cite_note-Zoladz-2024-94) accentuated by live drums and [melisma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melisma "Melisma") vocals.[\[77\]](#cite_note-Kornhaber-78)[\[91\]](#cite_note-95) The intricate arrangement of "Who's Afraid of Little Old Me?" resembles [orchestral pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orchestral_pop "Orchestral pop"): deep layers of dense, galloping synth [sequences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sequence_\(music\) "Sequence (music)"), grainy [Moog bass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moog_bass "Moog bass"), and a mix of electric guitar and drums.[\[42\]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTESomvilleBenoit2025449-42) "I Can Fix Him (No Really I Can)" is instrumented by sparse, tremolo guitars and percussion that sound like gunshots, evoking a [Wild West](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wild_West "Wild West") atmosphere and connotations of [western music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_music_\(North_America\) "Western music (North America)").[\[18\]](#cite_note-Savage-2024-18)[\[71\]](#cite_note-Molloy-2024-71)[\[92\]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTESomvilleBenoit2025450-96)

The minimalistic [piano ballad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piano_ballad "Piano ballad") "Loml" is driven by slow, melancholic piano chord [arpeggios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arpeggio "Arpeggio") and soft vocals, building up with strings towards the end, while "I Can Do It with a Broken Heart" is driven by frantic synth [arpeggiators](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arpeggiator "Arpeggiator") and throbbing bass programming over an upbeat [dance-pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dance-pop "Dance-pop"), electropop, and [disco-pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disco-pop "Disco-pop") sound.[\[93\]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTESomvilleBenoit2025441–442-97) "The Smallest Man Who Ever Lived" begins as a piano ballad and builds up with a monotone synth sequence and a climactic second part, instrumented with Swift's [distorted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Distortion_\(music\) "Distortion (music)") vocals over [eighth-note](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eighth-note "Eighth-note") [bass drums](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bass_drum "Bass drum") and [crescendoing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crescendo "Crescendo") orchestral strings.[\[94\]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTESomvilleBenoit2025453Zaleski2024-98) "The Alchemy" is a pop-rock song with uneven textures of electric guitars, [sixteenth-note](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sixteenth-note "Sixteenth-note") synth sequences, and [rhythm and blues](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhythm_and_blues "Rhythm and blues")\-styled acoustic drums,[\[95\]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTESomvilleBenoit2025454-99) and the minimalist chamber-pop and pop-rock song "Clara Bow" is instrumented with airy, _[staccato](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Staccato "Staccato")_ strings and dual bass: one [tonic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tonic_\(music\) "Tonic (music)"), and one that harmonizes.[\[96\]](#cite_note-100)[\[97\]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTESomvilleBenoit2025455-101)

_The Anthology_ is more musically uniformed, consisting of five piano ballads ("How Did It End?", "Cassandra", "Peter", "Robin", "The Manuscript"), two piano-led ballads ("The Black Dog", "Chloe or Sam or Sophia or Marcus"), and five guitar ballads propelled by [fingerpicking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fingerpicking "Fingerpicking") ("I Hate It Here", "Thank You Aimee", "I Look in People's Windows", "The Prophecy", "The Bolter").[\[98\]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTESomvilleBenoit2025467-102) There are a few outliers: "[Imgonnagetyouback](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imgonnagetyouback "Imgonnagetyouback")" has a synth-pop production and R&B-influenced vocals,[\[99\]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTESomvilleBenoit2025457-103) and "[So High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/So_High_School "So High School")" evokes 1990s rock styles such as indie rock and [alternative rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alternative_rock "Alternative rock"). "[The Albatross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Albatross_\(Taylor_Swift_song\) "The Albatross (Taylor Swift song)")" is a mid-tempo indie folk ballad.[\[83\]](#cite_note-Jenkins-87)[\[100\]](#cite_note-104)[\[101\]](#cite_note-105)

# The Tortured Poets Department

/en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J._M._Barrie "J. M. Barrie")'s 20th-century play and novel _[Peter Pan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Pan_\(play_and_novel\) "Peter Pan (play and novel)")_. Told from the perspective of [Wendy Darling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wendy_Darling "Wendy Darling"), the song depicts her waiting by the window for the day [Peter Pan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Pan_\(character\) "Peter Pan (character)") grows up and comes back to her. By the end of the song, in the [bridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bridge_\(music\) "Bridge (music)"), she concedes that she has tried in vain and, pleading with Peter Pan to forgive her, extinguishes the candlelight.[\[45\]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBurt2025-45)[\[55\]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMills2024237-55) "The Bolter" was influenced by [Nancy Mitford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Mitford "Nancy Mitford")'s 1945 novel _[The Pursuit of Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Pursuit_of_Love "The Pursuit of Love")_, about a female character nicknamed "The Bolter", who stays in society's margin and looks for love anywhere and in anyone. In her song, Swift's narrator is an endearing and mischievous woman who finds pleasure in seducing bad men, whom she describes as "trophy hunters", and escaping them at every turn.[\[48\]](#cite_note-Telegraph-48)[\[56\]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTESomvilleBenoit2025468-56)

Other tracks draw from Swift's self-awareness and fame. In "[How Did It End?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/How_Did_It_End%3F "How Did It End?")", her narrator explores anguish over a failed relationship and contemplates how the public's interest in her private life contributes to the distorted reality and gossip that ensue.[\[57\]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTESomvilleBenoit2025460-57) In "I Hate It Here", her narrator daydreams about escaping to an idealized past, imagining a beautiful landscape of secret gardens, lunar valleys, and gentle people, but she later acknowledges that nostalgia is a trap.[\[58\]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTESomvilleBenoit2025462-58) "[Thank You Aimee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thank_You_Aimee "Thank You Aimee")" is a sarcastic attack on a high-school bully; Swift's narrator appreciates the bully for making her stronger and tells them that she has changed their name so that they cannot enjoy the attention.[\[48\]](#cite_note-Telegraph-48) The closing track, "The Manuscript", is a re-examination of a long-gone romantic relationship with an older man; while it was once painful, Swift's narrator reflects on it with maturity and acceptance.[\[19\]](#cite_note-Wilson-2024-19)[\[48\]](#cite_note-Telegraph-48) She ends the song with the line, "The story isn't mine anymore." According to Mills, this lyric refers to the "[death of the author](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Death_of_the_author "Death of the author")"—by relinquishing authorship on her stories, Swift gives way for her audience to collectively construct and own theirs, thus positioning herself as a "modern-day Homer" and turning her songs into folktales.[\[55\]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMills2024237-55)

## Production and music

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=The_Tortured_Poets_Department&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Production and music")\]

_The Tortured Poets Department_ took two years to complete.[\[7\]](#cite_note-Martoccio-2024-7) Swift recorded and produced with Antonoff at [Electric Lady Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electric_Lady_Studios "Electric Lady Studios") in New York City and [Conway Recording Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conway_Recording_Studios "Conway Recording Studios") in Los Angeles, and with Dessner at Long Pond Studios in the [Hudson Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hudson_Valley "Hudson Valley"). "Fresh Out the Slammer", "Florida!!!", and "Who's Afraid of Little Old Me" were additionally recorded at Esplanade Studios in [New Orleans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Orleans "New Orleans"); "Florida!!!" also at [Miloco Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miloco_Studios "Miloco Studios") in London; and "I Can Fix Him (No Really I Can)" at Rue Boyer Studio A in [Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris "Paris").[\[9\]](#cite_note-Liner-9) On tracks co-produced with Antonoff, his bandmates from [Bleachers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bleachers_\(band\) "Bleachers (band)") played and recorded instruments at their respective studios: [Zem Audu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zem_Audu "Zem Audu") and [Evan Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evan_Smith_\(musician\) "Evan Smith (musician)") on [synthesizers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synthesizers "Synthesizers"), [Michael Riddleberger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Riddleberger "Michael Riddleberger") and [Sean Hutchinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Hutchinson "Sean Hutchinson") on drums and percussion, and [Mikey Freedom Hart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mikey_Freedom_Hart "Mikey Freedom Hart") on guitars and keyboards.[\[9\]](#cite_note-Liner-9)[\[59\]](#cite_note-59) Swift's vocals were recorded by Laura Sisk at Electric Lady, and by [Christopher Rowe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Rowe_\(music_producer\) "Christopher Rowe (music producer)") at Prime Recording Studio in [Nashville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nashville "Nashville").[\[9\]](#cite_note-Liner-9) Conducted by [Robert Ames](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Ames_\(conductor\) "Robert Ames (conductor)"), the [London Contemporary Orchestra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_Contemporary_Orchestra "London Contemporary Orchestra") provided [string sections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/String_section "String section") consisting of violins, violas, cellos, and [double basses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Double_bass "Double bass"), to "Clara Bow" on the standard edition,[\[60\]](#cite_note-60) and nine tracks on _The Anthology_.[\[61\]](#cite_note-61)

The music of _The Tortured Poets Department_ is [minimalist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minimalist_music "Minimalist music").[\[62\]](#cite_note-Keefe-2024-62)[\[63\]](#cite_note-Bannikov-63) Compositionally, the songs reprise many elements that had been characteristic of Swift's music: they employ the [verse-chorus form](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Verse-chorus_form "Verse-chorus form") largely composed in [major scale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_scale "Major scale") and set in [common time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Common_time "Common time"), one-note melodies in the verses that create tensions for more tuneful choruses, and [syncopated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syncopated "Syncopated") rhythms and phrasings.[\[64\]](#cite_note-Pareles-2024-64)[\[65\]](#cite_note-65) Many critics commented that the song structures and instrumental timbres feature influences of country music, a genre that defined her early career;[\[15\]](#cite_note-Brown-2024-15)[\[66\]](#cite_note-Petridis-66)[\[67\]](#cite_note-Foggart-67)[\[68\]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHughes2025132-68) according to [Jon Pareles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Pareles "Jon Pareles") of _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Times "The New York Times")_, Swift plays on traditional country songwriting by employing a "choppy pre-chorus, or chorus, that arrives in two-syllable bursts", which accentuates a steady verse structure and brings a "[hip-hop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hip-hop "Hip-hop") percussiveness".[\[64\]](#cite_note-Pareles-2024-64) Swift sings mostly in the lower ranges of her [vocal register](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vocal_register "Vocal register"), resulting in a [rap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rap "Rap")\-like, conversational delivery;[\[14\]](#cite_note-Powers-2024-14)[\[21\]](#cite_note-Leszkiewicz-21)[\[69\]](#cite_note-Breihan-2024-69) the music professor Samuel Murray commented that she reprised many of her common vocal devices, such as one-note melodies and a [recitative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recitative "Recitative") singing style.[\[36\]](#cite_note-Murray-36)

![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cb/Gnome-mime-audio-openclipart.svg/60px-Gnome-mime-audio-openclipart.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)

[electronica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronica "Electronica") soundscape composed of sustained [pads](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synth_pad "Synth pad") and [bass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synth_bass "Synth bass"),[\[15\]](#cite_note-Brown-2024-15)[\[21\]](#cite_note-Leszkiewicz-21)[\[74\]](#cite_note-Rogerson-2024-75) electronic [pulses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulse_\(music\) "Pulse (music)"),[\[23\]](#cite_note-Light-2024-23) and sparse, [programmed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Programming_\(music\) "Programming (music)") [drum machine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drum_machine "Drum machine") beats.[\[75\]](#cite_note-Horn-2024-76)[\[76\]](#cite_note-77) The compositions incorporate elements of country, [rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_music "Rock music"),[\[77\]](#cite_note-Kornhaber-78) [pop rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_rock "Pop rock"),[\[66\]](#cite_note-Petridis-66) [dream pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dream_pop "Dream pop"),[\[67\]](#cite_note-Foggart-67) and [sophisti-pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophisti-pop "Sophisti-pop").[\[78\]](#cite_note-Bridgewater-2024-79) According to music critics, _The Tortured Poets Department_ evokes the pop sounds of Swift's albums _Midnights_[\[b\]](#cite_note-80) and "Sentimental ballad")[\[63\]](#cite_note-Bannikov-63)[\[73\]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTESomvilleBenoit2025439-74)[\[80\]](#cite_note-83) that characterize _The Anthology_,[\[49\]](#cite_note-Sheffield-Anthology-49)[\[81\]](#cite_note-Exclaim!-84) which also infuses elements of [soft rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soft_rock "Soft rock").[\[82\]](#cite_note-85) Critics compared this production style to his collaborations with Swift on her 2020 albums _[Folklore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Folklore_\(Taylor_Swift_album\) The minimalistic [piano ballad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piano_ballad "Piano ballad") "Loml" is driven by slow, melancholic piano chord [arpeggios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arpeggio "Arpeggio") and soft vocals, building up with strings towards the end, while "I Can Do It with a Broken Heart" is driven by frantic synth [arpeggiators](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arpeggiator "Arpeggiator") and throbbing bass programming over an upbeat [dance-pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dance-pop "Dance-pop"), electropop, and [disco-pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disco-pop "Disco-pop") sound.[\[93\]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTESomvilleBenoit2025441–442-97) "The Smallest Man Who Ever Lived" begins as a piano ballad and builds up with a monotone synth sequence and a climactic second part, instrumented with Swift's [distorted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Distortion_\(music\) "Distortion (music)") vocals over [eighth-note](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eighth-note "Eighth-note") [bass drums](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bass_drum "Bass drum") and [crescendoing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crescendo "Crescendo") orchestral strings.[\[94\]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTESomvilleBenoit2025453Zaleski2024-98) "The Alchemy" is a pop-rock song with uneven textures of electric guitars, [sixteenth-note](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sixteenth-note "Sixteenth-note") synth sequences, and [rhythm and blues](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhythm_and_blues "Rhythm and blues")\-styled acoustic drums,[\[95\]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTESomvilleBenoit2025454-99) and the minimalist chamber-pop and pop-rock song "Clara Bow" is instrumented with airy, _[staccato](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Staccato "Staccato")_ strings and dual bass: one [tonic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tonic_\(music\) "Tonic (music)"), and one that harmonizes.[\[96\]](#cite_note-100)[\[97\]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTESomvilleBenoit2025455-101)

_The Anthology_ is more musically uniformed, consisting of five piano ballads ("How Did It End?", "Cassandra", "Peter", "Robin", "The Manuscript"), two piano-led ballads ("The Black Dog", "Chloe or Sam or Sophia or Marcus"), and five guitar ballads propelled by [fingerpicking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fingerpicking "Fingerpicking") ("I Hate It Here", "Thank You Aimee", "I Look in People's Windows", "The Prophecy", "The Bolter").[\[98\]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTESomvilleBenoit2025467-102) There are a few outliers: "[Imgonnagetyouback](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imgonnagetyouback "Imgonnagetyouback")" has a synth-pop production and R&B-influenced vocals,[\[99\]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTESomvilleBenoit2025457-103) and "[So High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/So_High_School "So High School")" evokes 1990s rock styles such as indie rock and [alternative rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alternative_rock "Alternative rock"). "[The Albatross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Albatross_\(Taylor_Swift_song\) "The Albatross (Taylor Swift song)")" is a mid-tempo indie folk ballad.[\[83\]](#cite_note-Jenkins-87)[\[100\]](#cite_note-104)[\[101\]](#cite_note-105)

A [vinyl-wrapped](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vehicle_vinyl_wrap "Vehicle vinyl wrap") [double decker bus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Double_decker_bus "Double decker bus") advertising the album in London, May 2024

Commenting on the title _The Tortured Poets Department_, Burt argued that while this did not turn Swift into a "print-based poet", it showcased her ability to incorporate evocative lyrics into pop songs.[\[32\]](#cite_note-BurtNation-32) The lack of an apostrophe, as in _The Tortured Poets' Department_, was the subject of a debate in the press over grammatical correctness.[\[102\]](#cite_note-106) Literary scholars commented that the title was grammatically correct: Swift used _Tortured Poets_ as an [attributive noun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attributive_noun "Attributive noun"), as in the title of the 1989 film _[Dead Poets Society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dead_Poets_Society "Dead Poets Society")_, and not as a [possessive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Possessive "Possessive") noun.[\[103\]](#cite_note-107)[\[104\]](#cite_note-108)

lobal 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Global_200 "Billboard Global 200"), marking Swift's fifth number-one song and tying her with [Bad Bunny](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Bunny "Bad Bunny") for the most chart toppers among solo acts. It was one of the nine tracks from _The Tortured Poets Department_ to debut within the top 10, extending Swift's number of top-10 entries to 33.[\[78\]](#cite_note-81)

In the United States, "Fortnight" debuted at number 9 on [Adult Pop Airplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adult_Pop_Airplay "Adult Pop Airplay") and number 13 on [Pop Airplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_Airplay "Pop Airplay"). It tied her own "[Shake It Off](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shake_It_Off "Shake It Off")" (2014) as the highest debut on the former chart, and "[Bad Blood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Blood_\(Taylor_Swift_song\) "Bad Blood (Taylor Swift song)")" (2015) as the second-highest debut on the latter chart.[\[79\]](#cite_note-82) On the Adult Pop Airplay chart dated June 22, 2024, the single reached number one to become Swift's record-extending 13th chart topper and Malone's second.[\[80\]](#cite_note-83) On the [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100"), "Fortnight" debuted at number one on the chart dated May 4, 2024. As Swift's 12th number-one single and seventh number-one debut, it tied Swift with [Ariana Grande](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ariana_Grande "Ariana Grande") for the [most number-one debuts for a female artist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Billboard_Hot_100_chart_achievements_and_milestones#Most_number-one_debuts "List of Billboard Hot 100 chart achievements and milestones"). "Fortnight" also marked Malone's fifth number-one single and first number-one debut.[\[81\]](#cite_note-84) The single spent two consecutive weeks atop the Hot 100.[\[82\]](#cite_note-85)

"Fortnight" is Swift's fourth number-one single in the United Kingdom and 12th in Australia.[\[83\]](#cite_note-86)[\[84\]](#cite_note-87) The single also topped the charts in Canada, Singapore, and the United Arab Emirates,[\[85\]](#cite_note-Canada-88)[\[86\]](#cite_note-Singapore-89)[\[87\]](#cite_note-MENA-90) as well as _Billboard_'s [Hits of the World](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hits_of_the_World "Hits of the World") charts for [Hong Kong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hong_Kong_Songs "Hong Kong Songs"), [Malaysia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malaysia_Songs "Malaysia Songs"), and [the Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippines_Songs "Philippines Songs").[\[88\]](#cite_note-Hong_Kong-91)[\[89\]](#cite_note-MalaysiaBB-92)[\[90\]](#cite_note-Philippines-93) It peaked at number two on the chart for the [Middle East and North Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middle_East_and_North_Africa "Middle East and North Africa") (MENA) region,[\[87\]](#cite_note-MENA-90) and charted within the top five of _Billboard_'s Hits of the World charts for Taiwan and Indonesia.[\[91\]](#cite_note-Taiwan-94)[\[92\]](#cite_note-Indonesia-95) Across Europe, "Fortnight" reached number two in Austria, Denmark, Germany, and Portugal;[\[93\]](#cite_note-denmark-96)[\[94\]](#cite_note-germany-97)[\[95\]](#cite_note-AUT-98)[\[96\]](#cite_note-Portugal-99) number three in Switzerland;[\[97\]](#cite_note-switzerland-100) number four in [Flanders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flanders "Flanders"), Latvia, Lithuania, Norway, and Sweden;[\[98\]](#cite_note-flanders-101)[\[99\]](#cite_note-Latvia-102)[\[100\]](#cite_note-Lithuania-103)[\[101\]](#cite_note-norway-104)[\[102\]](#cite_note-sweden-105) number five in Iceland;[\[103\]](#cite_note-Iceland-106) and the top 10 in Slovakia, the Netherlands, and the Czech Republic.[\[104\]](#cite_note-slovakia-107)[\[105\]](#cite_note-netherlands-108)[\[106\]](#cite_note-czech-109) The single has been [certified](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_recording_certifications "Music recording certifications") diamond in Brazil,[\[107\]](#cite_note-brazilcert-110) five-times platinum in Australia,[\[108\]](#cite_note-ARIA-111) double platinum in New Zealand,[\[109\]](#cite_note-RMNZ-112) and platinum in Belgium,[\[110\]](#cite_note-BEA-113) France,[\[111\]](#cite_note-SNEP-114) Poland,[\[112\]](#cite_note-Poland-115) Portugal,[\[113\]](#cite_note-ABP-116) Spain,[\[114\]](#cite_note-PROMUSICAE-117) Switzerland,[\[115\]](#cite_note-IFPISWI-118) and the United Kingdom.[\[116\]](#cite_note-BPI-119)

Swift wrote and directed the music video for "Fortnight", whose cinematography was handled by the Mexican filmmaker [Rodrigo Prieto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rodrigo_Prieto "Rodrigo Prieto").[\[117\]](#cite_note-IndieWire-120) According to Swift, the music video for "Fortnight" was the visual representation of _The Tortured Poets Department_: "Pretty much everything in it is a metaphor or a reference to one corner of the album or another."[\[118\]](#cite_note-Murphy-2024-121)

Four hours prior to the album's release, Swift posted a teaser for the music video on social media.[\[119\]](#cite_note-122) The music video was released on April 19, 2024.[\[120\]](#cite_note-123) It has a black-and-white cinematography and features Swift and Malone as ex-lovers, and _[Dead Poets Society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dead_Poets_Society "Dead Poets Society")_'s co-stars [Ethan Hawke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethan_Hawke "Ethan Hawke") and [Josh Charles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josh_Charles "Josh Charles") as [mad scientists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mad_scientist "Mad scientist") carrying out tests on Swift.[\[117\]](#cite_note-IndieWire-120)[\[121\]](#cite_note-EW-124) Malone recalled that Swift had to hide under an umbrella and drapes "over the golf cart so drones and a helicopter couldn't get footage" during filming of the video.[\[6\]](#cite_note-Coscarelli-2024-6)

[![An exhibit of a black Victorian-gothic gown](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c3/Taylor_Swift_Songbook_Trail_Fortnight_display_05.jpg/250px-Taylor_Swift_Songbook_Trail_Fortnight_display_05.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Taylor_Swift_Songbook_Trail_Fortnight_display_05.jpg)

Swift's black [Victorian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victorian_fashion "Victorian fashion")\-[gothic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gothic_fashion "Gothic fashion") ensemble gown from the music video, designed by [Elena Velez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elena_Velez "Elena Velez") (dress) and UNTTLD (top)[\[122\]](#cite_note-Sanchez-2024-125)

The video starts with Swift seen in a white dress and [choker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Choker "Choker"), chained to a bed in a mental facility;[\[123\]](#cite_note-Spanos-2024-126)[\[124\]](#cite_note-127) the bed is suspended on the wall.[\[25\]](#cite_note-Camp-2024-26) After a faceless person gives her a "Forget Him" pill, Swift wipes her face to reveal tattoos.[\[123\]](#cite_note-Spanos-2024-126)[\[125\]](#cite_note-West-2024-128) She walks into a room filled with [Royal 10 typewriters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_10 "Royal 10") with black-masked figures typing them,[\[122\]](#cite_note-Sanchez-2024-125)[\[126\]](#cite_note-129) donning a black [Victorian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victorian_fashion "Victorian fashion") mourning dress.[\[66\]](#cite_note-Power-2024-69) She sits and begins typing with Malone across the room.[\[123\]](#cite_note-Spanos-2024-126)[\[125\]](#cite_note-West-2024-128) Swift and Malone are then seen lying on top of a pile of papers, reading a book titled _Us_.[\[122\]](#cite_note-Sanchez-2024-125)[\[127\]](#cite_note-130) They embrace on a lone highway before being caught up in a tornado that causes loose papers to swirl around them.[\[123\]](#cite_note-Spanos-2024-126)[\[128\]](#cite_note-Thomas-2024-131)

Back at the mental facility, Swift is seen strapped to a gurney in a laboratory.[\[121\]](#cite_note-EW-124)[\[128\]](#cite_note-Thomas-2024-131) The doctors (Hawke and Charles) perform [electroshock therapy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electroshock_therapy "Electroshock therapy") on her as Malone watches from the side, before he unplugs the equipment to stop the procedure.[\[121\]](#cite_note-EW-124)[\[129\]](#cite_note-CosmopolitanMV-132) In the final scene, Malone calls from a telephone booth that Swift, in a sparkling [flapper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flapper "Flapper") dress,[\[130\]](#cite_note-Soo-2024-133) is on top of in the pouring thunderstorm rain, on an isolated cliff. He comes out of the booth and grabs Swift's hand.[\[125\]](#cite_note-West-2024-128) The video ends with silent-film credits.[\[118\]](#cite_note-Murphy-2024-121)

### Interpretations and reception

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Fortnight_\(song\)&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Interpretations and reception")\]

According to many publications, Swift's character in the video evokes the protagonist of the 2023 movie _[Poor Things](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poor_Things_\(film\) "Poor Things (film)"),_[\[d\]](#cite_note-136) and the scene of her being experimented on by mad scientists resembles [Mary Shelley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mary_Shelley "Mary Shelley")'s 1818 [gothic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gothic_fiction "Gothic fiction") novel _[Frankenstein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frankenstein "Frankenstein")_.[\[e\]](#cite_note-138) In the French film magazine [_Première_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Première_\(magazine\) "Première (magazine)"), Anthéa Claux compared the black-and-white cinematography and certain scenes to those of early-20th century [German expressionist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_expressionist_cinema "German expressionist cinema") silent films: the close-up scene showing Swift's face and makeup evokes [_Metropolis_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolis_\(1927_film\) "Metropolis (1927 film)") (1927), and the mental facility setting with its bed suspended on the wall and distorted interiors resembles the settings of _[The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Cabinet_of_Dr._Caligari "The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari")_ (1920).[\[133\]](#cite_note-Claux-2024-137)

Analyses of the video identified themes of mourning and reliving memories of a past relationship.[\[f\]](#cite_note-139) Fashion magazines examined Swift's fashion relating to Victorian and [gothic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gothic_fashion "Gothic fashion") styles that channeled poets and writers like Mary Shelley or [Emily Dickinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emily_Dickinson "Emily Dickinson").[\[g\]](#cite_note-142) Ed Power of _The Daily Telegraph_ thought that the video portrayed a haunting version of Swift that "gets under our skin like never before" and complimented the acting chemistry between Swift and Malone.[\[66\]](#cite_note-Power-2024-69) According to the literature professor Matthew J.A. Green, the video of "Fortnight" was part of Swift's foray into literary gothic, which was an important artistic endeavor that represented womanhood and the critique of one's self.[\[136\]](#cite_note-143)

At the [2024 MTV Video Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_MTV_Video_Music_Awards "2024 MTV Video Music Awards"), Swift won seven trophies, five of which were for "Fortnight",[\[137\]](#cite_note-Atkinson-2024-144) becoming the most-awarded artist in a single night in the awards' history.[\[138\]](#cite_note-145) Its trophy for [Video of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Video_Music_Award_for_Video_of_the_Year "MTV Video Music Award for Video of the Year") extended Swift's record as the artist with the most wins (five times).[\[139\]](#cite_note-146) "Fortnight" also won [Best Video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Europe_Music_Award_for_Best_Video "MTV Europe Music Award for Best Video") at the [2024 MTV Europe Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_MTV_Europe_Music_Awards "2024 MTV Europe Music Awards"),[\[140\]](#cite_note-147) and for his cinematography work, Prieto won the Grand Prize (Golden Frog) in the Music Videos category at the [32nd International Film Festival of the Art of Cinematography Camerimage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/32nd_International_Film_Festival_of_the_Art_of_Cinematography_Camerimage "32nd International Film Festival of the Art of Cinematography Camerimage").[\[141\]](#cite_note-148)

Credits are adapted from the [liner notes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liner_notes "Liner notes") of _The Tortured Poets Department_.[\[23\]](#cite_note-liner-24)

*   [Jack Antonoff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Antonoff "Jack Antonoff") – producer, songwriter, drums, [Juno](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roland_Juno-60 "Roland Juno-60"), [M1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korg_M1 "Korg M1"), percussion, electric guitar, acoustic guitar, [programming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Programming_\(music\) "Programming (music)")
*   [Louis Bell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_Bell "Louis Bell") – vocal producer, vocal engineer
*   [Serban Ghenea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serban_Ghenea "Serban Ghenea") – [mixing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Audio_mixing_\(recorded_music\) "Audio mixing (recorded music)")
*   Bryce Bordone – mix engineer
*   Laura Sisk – recording engineer

Four hours prior to the album's release, Swift posted a teaser for the music video on social media.[\[119\]](#cite_note-122) The music video was released on April 19, 2024.[\[120\]](#cite_note-123) It has a black-and-white cinematography and features Swift and Malone as ex-lovers, and _[Dead Poets Society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dead_Poets_Society "Dead Poets Society")_'s co-stars [Ethan Hawke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethan_Hawke "Ethan Hawke") and [Josh Charles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josh_Charles "Josh Charles") as [mad scientists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mad_scientist "Mad scientist") carrying out tests on Swift.[\[117\]](#cite_note-IndieWire-120)[\[121\]](#cite_note-EW-124) Malone recalled that Swift had to hide under an umbrella and drapes "over the golf cart so drones and a helicopter couldn't get footage" during filming of the video.[\[6\]](#cite_note-Coscarelli-2024-6)

[![An exhibit of a black Victorian-gothic gown](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c3/Taylor_Swift_Songbook_Trail_Fortnight_display_05.jpg/250px-Taylor_Swift_Songbook_Trail_Fortnight_display_05.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Taylor_Swift_Songbook_Trail_Fortnight_display_05.jpg)

Swift's black [Victorian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victorian_fashion "Victorian fashion")\-[gothic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gothic_fashion "Gothic fashion") ensemble gown from the music video, designed by [Elena Velez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elena_Velez "Elena Velez") (dress) and UNTTLD (top)[\[122\]](#cite_note-Sanchez-2024-125)

The video starts with Swift seen in a white dress and [choker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Choker "Choker"), chained to a bed in a mental facility;[\[123\]](#cite_note-Spanos-2024-126)[\[124\]](#cite_note-127) the bed is suspended on the wall.[\[25\]](#cite_note-Camp-2024-26) After a faceless person gives her a "Forget Him" pill, Swift wipes her face to reveal tattoos.[\[123\]](#cite_note-Spanos-2024-126)[\[125\]](#cite_note-West-2024-128) She walks into a room filled with [Royal 10 typewriters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_10 "Royal 10") with black-masked figures typing them,[\[122\]](#cite_note-Sanchez-2024-125)[\[126\]](#cite_note-129) donning a black [Victorian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victorian_fashion "Victorian fashion") mourning dress.[\[66\]](#cite_note-Power-2024-69) She sits and begins typing with Malone across the room.[\[123\]](#cite_note-Spanos-2024-126)[\[125\]](#cite_note-West-2024-128) Swift and Malone are then seen lying on top of a pile of papers, reading a book titled _Us_.[\[122\]](#cite_note-Sanchez-2024-125)[\[127\]](#cite_note-130) They embrace on a lone highway before being caught up in a tornado that causes loose papers to swirl around them.[\[123\]](#cite_note-Spanos-2024-126)[\[128\]](#cite_note-Thomas-2024-131)

Back at the mental facility, Swift is seen strapped to a gurney in a laboratory.[\[121\]](#cite_note-EW-124)[\[128\]](#cite_note-Thomas-2024-131) The doctors (Hawke and Charles) perform [electroshock therapy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electroshock_therapy "Electroshock therapy") on her as Malone watches from the side, before he unplugs the equipment to stop the procedure.[\[121\]](#cite_note-EW-124)[\[129\]](#cite_note-CosmopolitanMV-132) In the final scene, Malone calls from a telephone booth that Swift, in a sparkling [flapper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flapper "Flapper") dress,[\[130\]](#cite_note-Soo-2024-133) is on top of in the pouring thunderstorm rain, on an isolated cliff. He comes out of the booth and grabs Swift's hand.[\[125\]](#cite_note-West-2024-128) The video ends with silent-film credits.[\[118\]](#cite_note-Murphy-2024-121)

### Interpretations and reception

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Fortnight_\(song\)&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Interpretations and reception")\]

According to many publications, Swift's character in the video evokes the protagonist of the 2023 movie _[Poor Things](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poor_Things_\(film\) "Poor Things (film)"),_[\[d\]](#cite_note-136) and the scene of her being experimented on by mad scientists resembles [Mary Shelley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mary_Shelley "Mary Shelley")'s 1818 [gothic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gothic_fiction "Gothic fiction") novel _[Frankenstein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frankenstein "Frankenstein")_.[\[e\]](#cite_note-138) In the French film magazine [_Première_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Première_\(magazine\) "Première (magazine)"), Anthéa Claux compared the black-and-white cinematography and certain scenes to those of early-20th century [German expressionist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_expressionist_cinema "German expressionist cinema") silent films: the close-up scene showing Swift's face and makeup evokes [_Metropolis_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolis_\(1927_film\) "Metropolis (1927 film)") (1927), and the mental facility setting with its bed suspended on the wall and distorted interiors resembles the settings of _[The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Cabinet_of_Dr._Caligari "The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari")_ (1920).[\[133\]](#cite_note-Claux-2024-137)

Analyses of the video identified themes of mourning and reliving memories of a past relationship.[\[f\]](#cite_note-139) Fashion magazines examined Swift's fashion relating to Victorian and [gothic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gothic_fashion "Gothic fashion") styles that channeled poets and writers like Mary Shelley or [Emily Dickinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emily_Dickinson "Emily Dickinson").[\[g\]](#cite_note-142) Ed Power of _The Daily Telegraph_ thought that the video portrayed a haunting version of Swift that "gets under our skin like never before" and complimented the acting chemistry between Swift and Malone.[\[66\]](#cite_note-Power-2024-69) According to the literature professor Matthew J.A. Green, the video of "Fortnight" was part of Swift's foray into literary gothic, which was an important artistic endeavor that represented womanhood and the critique of one's self.[\[136\]](#cite_note-143)

At the [2024 MTV Video Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_MTV_Video_Music_Awards "2024 MTV Video Music Awards"), Swift won seven trophies, five of which were for "Fortnight",[\[137\]](#cite_note-Atkinson-2024-144) becoming the most-awarded artist in a single night in the awards' history.[\[138\]](#cite_note-145) Its trophy for [Video of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Video_Music_Award_for_Video_of_the_Year "MTV Video Music Award for Video of the Year") extended Swift's record as the artist with the most wins (five times).[\[139\]](#cite_note-146) "Fortnight" also won [Best Video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Europe_Music_Award_for_Best_Video "MTV Europe Music Award for Best Video") at the [2024 MTV Europe Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_MTV_Europe_Music_Awards "2024 MTV Europe Music Awards"),[\[140\]](#cite_note-147) and for his cinematography work, Prieto won the Grand Prize (Golden Frog) in the Music Videos category at the [32nd International Film Festival of the Art of Cinematography Camerimage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/32nd_International_Film_Festival_of_the_Art_of_Cinematography_Camerimage "32nd International Film Festival of the Art of Cinematography Camerimage").[\[141\]](#cite_note-148)

“Every year ends, and I think to myself, ‘That was a little crazy!’ ” Jack Antonoff says with a laugh. “It shouldn’t feel familiar, but it does.” That’s because the 39-year-old [studio](https://www.billboard.com/t/studio/) polymath has rarely experienced a quiet 12-month period over the past decade, juggling multiple production and songwriting projects while fronting his own band, Bleachers.

### Explore

[

![](https://www.billboard.com/wp-content/themes/vip/pmc-billboard-2021/assets/public/lazyload-fallback.gif)

](https://www.billboard.com/artist/jack-antonoff/)

See latest videos, charts and news

During the past year, Antonoff has helped produce [Taylor Swift](https://www.billboard.com/t/taylor-swift/)’s mega-selling _Midnights_, Lana Del Rey’s sweeping _Did You Know That There’s a Tunnel Under Ocean Blvd_ and The 1975’s ultra-catchy _Being Funny in a Foreign Language_, while also prepping Bleachers’ fourth full-length. He has signed a new label deal with Dirty Hit Records, brought in label founder Jamie Oborne as manager and inked a new deal with Universal Music Publishing Group. (“It doesn’t feel like anything’s shaken up, just that the team’s got a couple new members,” Antonoff says of the moves.) All the while, he’s eyeing a potential fifth consecutive producer of the year, non-classical Grammy nomination and third straight win, which would be the first three-peat in the category this century should it occur.

Two years ago, Antonoff shared with _Billboard_ his [seven habits of highly effective producers](https://www.billboard.com/music/pop/jack-antonoff-producers-now-digital-cover-interview-9603256/). As he hunkers down in the studio for the next few months — finishing Bleachers’ follow-up to 2021’s _Take the Sadness Out of Saturday Night_ and generally “chipping away at stuff” — he revealed his latest takeaways from his past year’s work.

### **Don’t Let Commercial Gains Distract in a Creative Space**

_Case study: Taylor Swift, “Anti-Hero”_

_Midnights_ scored the biggest [Billboard 200](https://www.billboard.com/charts/billboard-200/) debut of Swift’s career and her Eras Tour became the summer’s hottest stadium ticket, but Antonoff says that he marvels at how his frequent collaborator keeps her level of superstardom very much outside the studio. “There’s not a lot of panning back in the room — ‘Whoa, look at this \[achievement\], look at that!’ — because that would feel like popping the balloon,” he explains. “When I work with Taylor, there’s still just this person who has these life experiences and this remarkable gift of writing about them.”

See: “Anti-Hero,” the lead single from _Midnights_ that sardonically prods at Swift’s insecurities. “When we made ‘Anti-Hero,’ I just thought, ‘Wow, that’s so honest and funny, and also so sweet and so sad,’ ” Antonoff recalls, adding that the song, which became Swift’s longest-leading [Hot 100](https://www.billboard.com/charts/hot-100/) chart-topper earlier this year, wouldn’t have worked if they had been preoccupied by her radio appeal during its creation. “It has this weird beat going through a tremolo — no part of me was like, ‘F–king A, that’s the song to take over the world!’ ”

### **Sometimes the Spark Takes Time**…

_Case study: The 1975, “Part of the Band”_

“Who would you want to work with?” It’s a question Antonoff often hears, and one he finds impossible to answer. “I can only want to work with someone based on knowing them and seeing where they’re going,” he says. When Antonoff met The 1975, he envisioned a creative partnership where he could add to the band’s sound on its fifth album — but still experienced “that weird kind of early-relationship stuff” on _Being Funny in a Foreign Language_, his first project with the British rock group.

“Part of the Band,” the restrained, stream-of-consciousness lead single, helped alleviate some of that awkwardness. “It wasn’t the first thing we did,” Antonoff recalls, “but there’s a big difference between the first thing you do and the moment that you’re like, ‘Oh, sh-t. We have _that_ ability.’ Anyone can get in a room and carve out a song and make it sound halfway cool, but the idea of collaborating with people is doing something bigger than the sum of the parts.” Ultimately, “Part of the Band” unlocked the rest of _Being Funny in a Foreign Language_, which spun off five top 40 hits on the [Hot Rock & Alternative Songs](https://www.billboard.com/charts/rock-songs/) chart.

### …And Sometimes a Hit Can Take a _Really_ Long Time

_Case study: Taylor Swift, “Cruel Summer”_

“That was always one of my favorite songs I’d ever done,” Antonoff says of Swift’s _Lover_ standout, a synth-[pop](https://www.billboard.com/t/pop/) fantasia that became a fan favorite upon the 2019 album’s release. “Cruel Summer” didn’t become a hit single during the _Lover_ album cycle, which was curtailed due to the pandemic, and Antonoff made peace with its cult-classic status. But earlier this year, as the song became the centerpiece of the opening of Swift’s mega-selling Eras tour, “Cruel Summer” began soaring in streams, then in radio play, and climbed all the way to No. 3 on the Hot 100, morphing into one of the defining songs of the summer of 2023.

“It was just like, a huge thumbs-up from the universe,” Antonoff says of the song’s viral resurgence this year. “I take it all as a reminder to do what you believe in, make the songs you believe in. You never want to do anything that you don’t believe in for the sake of success, because the only thing worse than doing something you don’t believe in is being recognized for that thing! … With \[‘Cruel Summer’\], I loved that it existed, and didn’t need anything more from it. It’s just this bizarre icing on the cake.”

### **Ambition Comes in Many Forms**

_Case study: Lana Del Rey, “A&W”_

Antonoff says that his most frequent collaborators share the characteristic of “becoming obsessed with understanding what their ambition is and how to access it constantly” rather than resting on their laurels. That creative curiosity manifests itself in different ways: For Swift, after the indie-folk storytelling on _folklore_ and _evermore_ in 2020, “There was this sense of blazing out of the cabin” with the personal pop of _Midnights_. Meanwhile, The 1975 came to Antonoff after several winding, esoteric full-lengths, and he helped push _Being Funny in a Foreign Language_ into uncharted territory for the band: a tight, interlude-free pop-rock record.

For Del Rey’s _Did You Know That There’s a Tunnel Under Ocean Blvd_, the seven-minute centerpiece, “A&W” — which begins as a folk lament before flipping into a trap refrain midway through — resulted from experimenting with other album tracks like “Peppers” and “Taco Truck x VB,” mashing up sounds until arriving at the most innovative structure possible, according to Antonoff. “This sprawling thing was the most ambitious thing to do. A song like ‘A&W’ is just an example of what happens when you just know people so well that you can really support each other into strange places.”

### **Make an Entrance**

_Case study: Bleachers, “Modern Girl”_

Bleachers’ upcoming fourth album, which Antonoff and his six-piece group made with co-producer Patrik Berger and a few special guests, translates the jubilance of the band’s live show into a studio setting. Not every song is as boisterous as “Modern Girl,” released in September as the project’s lead single, but for Antonoff, its 1980s-indebted mix of jittery vocal energy and uncorked saxophone blasts captured “enough left-field sh-t that speaks to where the album is going” and was the obvious introduction.

“Putting out albums is like pulling at both the past and the future, and ‘Modern Girl’ just felt like this perfect shock and comfort moment, both honoring where Bleachers has been and where it’s going,” he says of the new album, due next year. “I’ve always believed in this ‘house’ mentality of just understanding what an album is, and ‘Modern Girl’ just feels like the biggest front door.”

[_A version of this story originally appeared in the Oct. 7, 2023, issue of_ Billboard.](https://shop.billboard.com/)
